findings.expected_benefit: Per linear layer at B sequences: ~25 + 35B launches -> ~25 + 35 + 4B. At conc=4 on Qwen3.5-4B-AWQ an estimated 25-35% higher aggregate throughput (toward the dense 2.7x scaling); at conc=8 proportionally more. No change at B=1.
findings.verify_how: conc=4 and conc=8 aggregate tok/s on Qwen3.5-4B-AWQ (README protocol) before/after; the battery's byte-identical batched-vs-single greedy check is the correctness gate (batched matmul order is identical per head, so bytes should match); add a unit test calling `forward_batch` with 3 states against three `forward_segment` calls.

verdict.reason: Verified gdn.rs:768-792: projections are batched once, then `mix_segment` runs per segment in the loop at :782-787 with `narrow().contiguous()` copies; block.rs:68-75 builds one `&mut Option<RecurrentState>` per segment. README:596-598 confirms the scaling numbers (24.6 -> 36.1, 1.5x, vs 2.7x dense). Batching is implementable: every op in `recurrent_delta_step` is a batched matmul or broadcast over the leading dim, `RecurrentState.s` is [h, dk, dv] F32 and `.conv` is [1, k-1, c] (paged.rs:969-974), and the conv t==1 path (:583-592) broadcasts `conv_w.unsqueeze(0)` over a leading batch; g/beta come out of `project` as [h, T] (:623-634) and need a transpose to [B*h, 1]. The cat/narrow cost is 2B x 2 MB per layer (B=4: ~770 MB per step over 24 layers, ~5 ms) against (B-1) x ~32 launches x 24 layers saved, so the net is positive at B>=2 and the pooled-state follow-up removes the copies. Risk to state: candle's Metal matmul may pick a different kernel for batch B*h than for h, so the battery's byte-identical batched-vs-single check may need a tolerance, or finding 8's kernel should land first so both paths share one reduction order. M effort honest.

findings.title: l2norm is five launches that the existing fused RMSNorm kernel computes exactly in one
findings.evidence: gdn.rs:114-117: `fn l2norm(x: &Tensor) -> Result<Tensor> { let sq = x.sqr()?.sum_keepdim(D::Minus1)?; x.broadcast_div(&(sq + L2_NORM_EPS)?.sqrt()?) }` called twice per step at :249-250 (`let q = (l2norm(q)? * (1.0 / (dk as f64).sqrt()))?; let k = l2norm(k)?;`) and twice per prefill at :279-280. metal_ops.rs:1286 `pub fn rms_norm_fused(x: &Tensor, weight: &Tensor, eps: f32)` with `rmsnorm_f32` at :342 accepting contiguous F32 `[.., last]` input and a `[last]` F32 weight; gdn.rs already uses it in `finish` (:731-735).
findings.rationale: rms_norm(x; w, e) = x * w / sqrt(sum(x^2)/d + e). Choosing e = 1e-6/d and w == 1/sqrt(d) gives exactly x / sqrt(sum(x^2) + 1e-6) = l2norm(x); for q, folding the dk^-0.5 scale gives w == 1/d. So both normalizations plus the q scale (11 launches per sequence per layer at decode: 5 + 5 + 1) become two fused launches with the same F32 arithmetic up to rounding. 24 layers x 9 = ~216 fewer launches per token (~2 ms, ~5% on the AWQ 4B) and the same in each prefill chunk. This is the interim step before finding 8, and costs nothing if finding 8 lands.
findings.proposal: At load, build two F32 weight vectors on the device: `w_k = [dk^-0.5; dk]` and `w_q = [1/dk; dk]`, store them in `GatedDeltaNet`, and in `recurrent_delta_step`/`chunk_gated_delta_rule` (pass them as arguments) use `rms_norm_fused(q.contiguous(), &w_q, (L2_NORM_EPS / dk as f64) as f32)` on Metal, falling back to the current `l2norm` on CPU. Note `(sum + eps)` vs `(mean + eps/d)`: identical algebraically; keep the fixture tolerance 1e-4.
findings.expected_benefit: -9 launches per sequence per linear layer at decode and per prefill chunk; ~5% decode on Qwen3.5-4B-AWQ at B=1, more at B>1 until finding 9 lands.
findings.verify_how: Run the gdn fixture tests on Metal (`Device::new_metal(0)` variant of `recurrent_step_matches_reference_and_chunked_prefill`) at 1e-4; `decode_ms` median on Qwen3.5-4B-AWQ before/after.

verdict.reason: Algebra checks: rms_norm(x; w, e) = x*w / sqrt(mean(x^2) + e); with e = 1e-6/d and w = d^-0.5 it equals x / sqrt(sum(x^2) + 1e-6), i.e. `l2norm` at gdn.rs:114-117 (L2_NORM_EPS = 1e-6 at :35); with w = 1/d it folds the dk^-0.5 scale of :249. `RmsNormOp` (metal_ops.rs, body at RmsNormOp+29..+62) accepts F32 x with F32 weight, any rank, contiguous, last_dim read from the layout, via `candle_metal_kernels::call_rms_norm`; q/k are contiguous after `to_heads`/`expand_heads` (:656-690) in decode and [h, t, dk] contiguous in `chunk_gated_delta_rule` (:279-280), so no extra copies. Saves 9 launches per linear layer per step (two 5-op norms plus the scale, replaced by two fused launches). Numerics differ at ULP level (rsqrt of mean+eps/d vs 1/sqrt(sum+eps)), covered by the 1e-4 fixture tolerance and deterministic. S effort honest; the Metal variant of the fixture test is the right gate.

findings.title: Chunked scan rebuilds and uploads its constant masks on every call (per linear layer per prefill chunk)
findings.evidence: gdn.rs:302-306 inside `chunk_gated_delta_rule`: `let g_c = cumsum_last(&pad2(g)?.reshape((hn, c))?, c)?; ... let tril = tril_mask(c, false, &device)?; let strict = tril_mask(c, true, &device)?;` where `tril_mask` (:128-136) and `cumsum_last` (:227-236) each fill a `vec![0f32; n*n]` on the CPU and `Tensor::from_vec` it; `invert_unit_lower_base` (:148) does `let id = eye(n, a.device())?` (:119-126) per call and `invert_unit_lower` (:215) allocates `Tensor::zeros((b*pairs, s, s))` per level.
findings.rationale: Four to six host-to-device allocations of fixed 64x64/16x16 F32 matrices per linear layer per prefill chunk (~150-220 per prefill on a 24-36-layer hybrid, more when the engine cuts prompts into pieces). Each is a pool allocation + memcpy on the engine thread, roughly 10-30 us; a few ms per prefill, and avoidable allocation churn in a pool whose exhaustion the ROADMAP identifies as dangerous.
findings.proposal: Cache `tril`, `strict`, the cumsum matrix `U`, `eye(16)` and `eye(64)` per device in `GatedDeltaNet` at load (device is known from the projections) or in a `OnceLock<Mutex<FxHashMap<(usize, DeviceId), Tensor>>>` keyed by n; pass them into `chunk_gated_delta_rule` / `invert_unit_lower`. The zero block in the blocked inversion can be replaced by `Tensor::cat` with a cached zero tile of each level size (two sizes for c=64).
findings.expected_benefit: Removes ~150-220 small allocations and uploads per prefill; a few ms of TTFT on hybrids, and less pool churn. Low, but mechanical.
findings.verify_how: Fixture tests unchanged (CPU); TTFT on a 1.3k-token prompt on Qwen3.5-4B before/after, and allocation count via `MTLDevice` capture or a counter in the pool.

findings.title: Causal embedder materializes an [heads, n, n] F32 score matrix and a host-built n^2 mask, bounded only by max_position_embeddings (32768)
findings.evidence: encoder.rs:430-434: `if n > self.max_positions { bail!(...) }` with `max_positions` from `config["max_position_embeddings"]...unwrap_or(32768)` (:367). :444-452: `let mask = { let mut data = vec![0f32; n * n]; for r in 0..n { for c in (r + 1)..n { data[r * n + c] = f32::NEG_INFINITY; } } Tensor::from_vec(data, (n, n), &self.device)? };`. :500-502: `let scores = (q.matmul(&k.transpose(2, 3)?)? * scale)?; let scores = scores.to_dtype(DType::F32)?.broadcast_add(&mask)?; let probs = softmax_last_dim(&scores)?.to_dtype(self.dtype)?;` with `q` shaped `[1, n_heads, n, head_dim]` (:468-476). `flash_attention_metal_prefill(q, k, v, scale, softcap, prefix_len, window)` exists at metal_ops.rs:1473 for BF16 and is causal by construction (`prefix_len + T_q == T_kv`).
findings.rationale: For Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B (16 heads) a 8192-token input allocates scores 4.3 GB (BF16 2.1 GB first), the F32 cast 4.3 GB, the masked sum 4.3 GB, the softmax 4.3 GB, the BF16 probs 2.1 GB, plus a 268 MB host mask built with an n^2 CPU loop and uploaded: ~15-20 GB of transient device allocations per request on a 24 GB machine, per layer in sequence. At 16k tokens each is 17 GB. The only guard is 32768. The ROADMAP records that Metal allocation failure has produced garbage rather than an error, so the consequence is a wrong embedding or a crashed server, on a model the README lists as verified. The bidirectional family is safe only because BERT's table is 512.
findings.proposal: (1) On Metal with BF16 route the causal embedder's attention through `flash_attention_metal_prefill(&q, &k, &v, scale, None, 0, 0)` (q/k/v already `[1, H, n, D]` contiguous; K/V expansion by `expand_kv` can stay or the kernel's GQA support be used), which removes the score matrix and the mask entirely. (2) Add a request cap: a server-side `max_embedding_tokens` (default e.g. 8192, flag/env twin) checked in `embeddings.rs` with a 400, and on CPU/fallback compute attention in query blocks of 512 rows with a per-block mask so peak memory is O(512 x n) instead of O(n^2).
findings.expected_benefit: Peak transient memory per embedding request drops from O(H n^2 x 4 B) to O(n x D); removes a silent-corruption/crash path on long documents; long-input embedding latency improves (FA kernel vs five full passes per layer).
findings.verify_how: Embed a 12k-token document on Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B on the M5 while watching memory; before: multi-GB spikes or failure, after: flat. Cosine against the sentence-transformers reference on the existing fixtures must stay > 0.999 (`causal_embedder_matches_sentence_transformers_reference`).

verdict.reason: Verified encoder.rs:430-434 (only guard is `max_positions`, defaulted to 32768 at :367), :444-452 (host n^2 F32 mask built in a double loop and uploaded), :468-476 (q as [1, H, n, D]), :500-502 (scores -> F32 -> broadcast_add -> softmax -> BF16: four full [H, n, n] tensors in flight). For Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B (16 heads, head_dim 128) at 8k tokens that is 2.1 GB BF16 + three 4.3 GB F32 tensors per layer, exactly the class of allocation failure the ROADMAP says turns into silent garbage. `flash_attention_metal_prefill` (metal_ops.rs:1473) takes [B, H, T, D] BF16, and `MppFlashAttn` supports GQA natively (bails only when n_heads is not divisible by n_kv_heads), so `expand_kv` can be dropped too; head_dim 128 is in the supported set and the non-mpp FA fallback exists. The encoder runs in the dtype passed from embeddings.rs:144, BF16 on Metal, so the fast path applies. Request cap + blocked CPU fallback are sensible. M effort honest.

findings.title: /v1/embeddings runs one full forward per input under the GPU lock; EncoderModel::embed has no batch interface
findings.evidence: encoder.rs:117 `pub fn embed(&self, ids: &[u32]) -> Result<Vec<f32>>` (dispatching to :249 and :425, each a single-sequence forward building `x` as `[n, hidden]`). embeddings.rs:59-68: `let _gpu = gpu.acquire(); ... for text in &batch { let ids = handle_for_embed.tokenizer.encode_with_special_tokens(text)?; prompt_tokens += ids.len(); vectors.push(handle_for_embed.model.embed(&ids)?); }`. The bidirectional path (:270-296) has no attention mask at all, so padding cannot be added without one.
findings.rationale: Bulk embedding (RAG indexing, the main use of this endpoint) sends tens to hundreds of short strings per request. Each becomes a full 12-28-layer forward of ~25-40 small launches per layer and a full read of the weights (granite 250 MB, Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B 1.2 GB), serialized on one blocking thread holding the GPU lock. For 64 strings of ~30 tokens that is 64 weight reads and ~20k launches where one padded forward would be 1 weight read and ~300 launches, and chat decode on the same device is blocked meanwhile.
findings.proposal: Add `embed_batch(&self, seqs: &[Vec<u32>]) -> Result<Vec<Vec<f32>>>`: sort by length, bucket into groups of similar length (cap e.g. 32 sequences or 8k total tokens), right-pad, and run one forward with (a) bidirectional: an additive key-padding mask `[B, 1, 1, L]` added before softmax, and mean-pooling that divides by real lengths; (b) causal: a combined causal + padding mask (or the FA kernel per finding 12 with per-sequence last-token gather via an index tensor). The route then calls `embed_batch` once; `usage.prompt_tokens` unchanged.
findings.expected_benefit: For requests of many short inputs, 5-20x throughput and proportionally less GPU-lock hold time (less interference with decode). No change for single-input requests.
findings.verify_how: Time a 64-string request on granite-embedding-125m and Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B before/after; assert per-string embeddings equal the single-sequence path to 1e-4 cosine (padding must not leak), which the existing fixture tests can check by embedding the fixture sentences together.

verdict.reason: Verified embeddings.rs:59-68: one `spawn_blocking`, `gpu.acquire()` held for the whole batch, and `model.embed(&ids)` per input; encoder.rs:117 dispatches to single-sequence forwards (:249-296 bidirectional, :425-510 causal), and the bidirectional attention at :286-287 has no mask at all, so padding cannot be introduced without adding one. Each input is a full weight read plus ~25-40 launches per layer, so for many short strings a padded batch is a large win and shortens GPU-lock hold time. One api-ux caveat to document: padded GEMM shapes change results at ULP level depending on which inputs are co-batched, so single-vs-batched vectors will not be bitwise equal (the sweep's 'bitwise-deterministic' check is run-to-run and holds if bucketing is deterministic). M effort honest; last-token gather per sequence is needed for the causal path.

findings.title: LayerNorm re-casts its weight and bias to F32 on every call
findings.evidence: encoder.rs:40-50: `fn forward(&self, x: &Tensor) -> Result<Tensor> { ... Ok(normed.broadcast_mul(&self.weight.to_dtype(DType::F32)?)?.broadcast_add(&self.bias.to_dtype(DType::F32)?)?.to_dtype(dtype)?) }`; `weight`/`bias` are stored in the load dtype (BF16 on Metal) at :29-37.
findings.rationale: Two cast launches per LayerNorm call, two LayerNorms per layer plus the embedding norm: ~50 extra launches per bidirectional forward out of roughly 350, on a path that is launch-bound for short inputs (granite-embedding is 125M parameters, ~250 MB, a ~2 ms weight read). Also seven separate ops for a norm that `rms_norm_fused`-style fusion would do in one, but the cast is the free part.
findings.proposal: Cast `weight` and `bias` to F32 once in `LayerNorm::load` and store them as F32 (they are tiny). Optionally add a fused LayerNorm Metal kernel next to `rms_norm_fused` later.
findings.expected_benefit: ~15% fewer launches per BERT-class forward; a few hundred microseconds per short input, which matters when the route loops per input (finding 13).
findings.verify_how: `encoder_matches_transformers_reference` cosine unchanged; per-request latency on granite-embedding for a 30-token string before/after.

findings.title: Encoder loader reads only model.safetensors, so sharded embedding checkpoints cannot load
findings.evidence: encoder.rs:195 `let weight_path = format!("{model_dir}/model.safetensors"); let weights = ModelWeights::load(&[weight_path.as_str()], device, dtype, None)?;` and identically at :369 for the causal embedder. `ModelWeights::load` takes a slice of paths (weights.rs:314-323 `MmapedSafetensors::multi(paths)`), so multi-shard is supported one line below.
findings.rationale: Qwen3-Embedding-4B and -8B (the larger siblings of the verified 0.6B, same `qwen3` model_type and same pooling config) ship as `model-0000X-of-0000N.safetensors` shards; the endpoint would fail with a file-not-found on exactly the models users upgrade to, with an error that does not say why.
findings.proposal: Resolve weights the way the decoder loader does: glob `model*.safetensors` in `model_dir` (or read `model.safetensors.index.json` when present), sort, and pass all paths to `ModelWeights::load`; error with a clear message when none is found.
findings.expected_benefit: Larger embedding models load; one less undocumented limitation of `/v1/embeddings`.
findings.verify_how: Pull Qwen3-Embedding-4B and call `/v1/embeddings`; compare cosine against sentence-transformers on the existing fixture sentences.

findings.title: Sparse dispatch is never tested with n_tokens > top_k or with inactive experts
findings.evidence: moe.rs:853-880 `naive_and_sparse_dispatch_agree`: `let (hidden, intermediate, num_experts, top_k) = (8, 16, 4, 2); ... // 2 tokens with top_k=2: n_tokens <= top_k -> forward takes the naive path; compute the sparse path directly`. With 2 tokens x top-2 of 4 experts almost every expert is active and `index_add` receives one or two rows. `moe_topk_routing_uses_only_topk_experts` (:738-760) only checks finiteness and a 10x magnitude band. No test runs `forward` on the sparse branch (`n_tokens > self.top_k`, :487) against a per-token reference.
findings.rationale: The prefill path (finding 3 proposes rewriting it) is only covered indirectly by E2E coherence checks on Metal. A CPU test that is cheap and exact would catch an un-permute or index bug immediately and makes the rewrite safe.
findings.proposal: Add `sparse_dispatch_matches_per_token_reference`: 32 tokens, 16 experts, top_k 2 (so ~half the experts are inactive and several get many rows), compute `moe.forward(x)` and compare against a loop that calls `dispatch_naive` on each token row separately (or sums `top_vals * expert.forward(row)` directly), tolerance 1e-5. Also assert that experts absent from `top_idx` are never resolved (wrap `ExpertBank::resolve` in a counting test double, or check `active.len()`).
findings.expected_benefit: Locks the sparse path's semantics before the index_add rewrite; near-zero runtime cost.
findings.verify_how: cargo test moe:: on CPU.

findings.title: Doc/code drift in the MoE and streaming modules: scatter_add gate, 'reusable scratch buffer', and a per-tensor drain only on the cast path
findings.evidence: moe.rs:20-24 module doc: 'build a dense `[n_tokens, num_experts]` gate via `scatter_add`, then for each non-empty expert run its FFN' — `dispatch_naive` (:549-597) builds per-expert CPU weight vectors, no scatter_add. expert_stream.rs:7 'straight into a reusable scratch buffer' vs `read_one` :420 `let mut bytes = vec![0u8; len as usize]`. expert_stream.rs:466-477 `fn to_device(..) { ... let dev = cpu.to_device(&self.device)?; drain_metal(&self.device, name)...; Ok(dev) }` drains per tensor on the cast path only, while the `no_cast` path (:443-447) and the `Fp8Resident` build (:508-520) upload without draining, and the `fetch_many` doc (:229-246) states uploads 'need no synchronization' and that 'the one Metal drain per batch happens after evictions'.
findings.rationale: The ROADMAP and these files are the maintainer's own map of what was measured; stale descriptions of the decode path ('dense gate') already misled the ROADMAP's wording of the MoE decode item. The asymmetric drain is either a leftover (then it costs one pipeline sync per cast tensor on non-BF16 checkpoints streamed to Metal, inside a rayon worker) or a real hazard the other two paths lack; either way the three paths should agree, and the comment should say which.
findings.proposal: Rewrite moe.rs:17-37 to describe the CPU-side routing + per-expert loop and the actual crossover; fix expert_stream.rs:7 (or implement finding 7); decide on the drain: if `new_buffer_with_data` is a synchronous copy (as the fetch_many doc asserts and the other paths rely on), delete the `drain_metal` in `to_device`; otherwise add it to the other two paths and document why.
findings.expected_benefit: Correct map for the next round of MoE work; removes one needless GPU sync per cast tensor on the F16/F8-without-scale streamed paths.
findings.verify_how: Code review; for the drain, run the streamed byte-identity check on a non-BF16 checkpoint (or the synthetic test with a Metal device) with the drain removed.

subsystems.coverage_notes: Read in full: src/common/moe.rs, src/common/gdn.rs, src/common/expert_stream.rs, src/models/encoder.rs. Read partially to confirm call paths and mechanisms: src/server/routes/embeddings.rs (1-140), src/common/block.rs (50-100, the GDN/MoE dispatch), src/common/weights.rs (metal_alloc_lock, drain_metal, ModelWeights::load phases), src/common/linear.rs (matmul_with_bias, softmax_last_dim, PackedQuantLinear gemv thresholds), src/common/mxfp4.rs (forward), src/common/metal_ops.rs (rms_norm_fused/silu_mul_fused/f8_gemv/f8_block_dequant_bf16 signatures, RmsNormOp dtype checks, flash_attention_metal_prefill), src/common/paged.rs (RecurrentState), src/models/loader.rs (1105-1125 and the lifetime of `weights`), src/engine.rs (grep: prefix cache and speculative decoding are gated off for recurrent models), README benchmark/env-var sections, CHANGELOG top, ROADMAP sections (done list, constant/flag audit, performance backlog, rejected), and candle-core 0.11.0 metal_backend (to_cpu, index_add) and sort.rs. Not covered: the bodies of the Metal kernels (mxfp4_matmul, f8_gemv, FlashAttn) and whether Mxfp4Matmul honours a tensor start offset (relevant to finding 5's cheapest variant); candle-metal-kernels' index_add kernel body (the full-copy claim rests on candle-core's index_add wrapper, which is sufficient); the engine's prefill chunking and preemption interplay with RecurrentState beyond the gdn unit tests; whether Qwen3-Embedding-4B is actually sharded (finding 15 is certain about the code limitation, less about which checkpoints hit it); the O(N) LRU victim scan in fetch_many (:297-302) was judged immaterial (<1% of a streamed token) and left out; OXYDLLM_GDN_CHUNK no longer exists and OXYDLLM_GDN_DEBUG is documented in README and guarded by a OnceLock, so the ROADMAP's flag concern is resolved and was not reported. Nothing was executed (no cargo, no Metal); all per-token launch counts are derived from reading the op sequences and are estimates to be measured on the M5, and all throughput bounds use the README/maintainer numbers as baselines.
missed: The streamed bank re-streams the entire expert set from SSD once per prefill chunk, and nothing in the chunk planner knows it. At prefill `MoeFeedForward::forward` takes `dispatch_sparse` (moe.rs:488-492), which calls `self.experts.resolve(&active)` (moe.rs:634) with up to every expert of the layer; for the Streamed bank that is `fetch_many` (expert_stream.rs:249-262), and its eviction loop (expert_stream.rs:297-308, `while state.bytes > self.cache_bytes && state.cache.len() > ids.len()`) keeps only the current layer's batch, so with a 3.4 GB cache against ~40 layers x 256 experts of F8 bytes every layer's experts are gone before the next chunk reaches that layer. TTFT for a streamed MoE is therefore (number of prefill chunks) x (total expert bytes / SSD bandwidth), i.e. a 4-chunk prompt costs four full passes over ~30-60 GB of expert data on top of the compute, which dwarfs every per-expert device inefficiency the reviewer found (findings 3, 4, 6). The engine's `PrefillPacer` (engine.rs:525-601) sizes chunks from measured time per chunk and the loader already decides streaming automatically, so the cheap fix is a hint from the model to the planner: when any layer holds a Streamed bank, prefer the largest chunk the memory envelope permits (ideally the whole prompt) instead of the pacer's generic cap, and let the pacer only shrink on failure. I did not read the pacer's cap logic, so the exact integration point is unverified, but the mechanism on the moe/expert_stream side is read in full. Verify on the M5 by timing TTFT on a 2k-token prompt for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 at the pinned 3400 MB cache with the pool's hit-rate log before and after.

subsystems.assessment: The quant-formats layer is in good shape where it counts: every layout conversion (compressed-tensors to AWQ, GPTQ PlusOne, AWQ interleave, RTN) is explicit, round-trip tested against an independent packer, and the resident kernels are checked against these CPU oracles; the HF parser is tolerant of missing fields, contract-tested on the awkward configs (Gemma 3 window period, Gemma 4 per-type rotary factors, text_config nesting), and refuses unsupported quant variants at parse time with actionable messages. What is fragile is the load-time choreography rather than the math: packed tensors are uploaded to Metal in ModelWeights::load and then, per layer, read back to the CPU for compressed-tensors conversion and again for q/k/v and gate/up fusion, re-uploaded, while the originals stay alive in the weights map until the loader returns, so a 4-bit model holds roughly 1.65x its packed bytes on device at peak and moves several GB across the bus for nothing. The Option A tied-lm_head quantization is the single biggest remaining decode lever on this subsystem and it is gated narrower than the maintainer's own note intended: GPTQ-Int4 tied checkpoints (the Qwen2.5 <=3B line) still read a BF16 lm_head that is ~30% of their per-token bytes, and the verified GPTQ-Int8 Qwen3 models have no 8-bit counterpart at all. Validation trusts config flags rather than tensor evidence: desc_act defaults to false when absent and g_idx is never read, so an act-order GPTQ file with a stale flag decodes garbage silently. The IQ decoder module is test-only and is the sole oracle for three Metal kernels, yet it is itself verified only by a magnitude heuristic, so a shared mapping error would be invisible to the whole chain. Config parsing is duplicated three times with opposite text_config precedence between the parser and estimate.rs. None of these is a correctness bug on the sweep-verified models; they are the headroom: +15-25% decode on GPTQ-4 tied models for a one-line gate change, a few seconds and ~1.6 GB of peak memory off packed-model loads by converting and fusing in the CPU phase, and cheap evidence-based checks that turn silent garbage into load errors.

findings.title: Option A tied-lm_head RTN gate excludes GPTQ-Int4, leaving a BF16 lm_head that is ~30% of per-token bytes on tied GPTQ-4 models
findings.evidence: awq.rs:656-657 `#[cfg(any(feature = "metal", test))] pub fn rtn_quantize_awq(weight: &Tensor, group_size: usize) -> Result<AwqRawTensors>` produces a PackDim::Out 4-bit triplet that `AnyLinear::from_awq` (linear.rs:552-569) turns into a PackedQuantLinear independent of the model's own scheme. The only caller gates it at loader.rs:1234-1243: `if has_packed_quantized_weights && device.is_metal() && matches!(dtype, F16|BF16) && matches!(weights.quant_scheme(), Some(QuantScheme::Awq { bits: 4 }) | Some(QuantScheme::CompressedTensors4))`. `QuantScheme::Gptq { bits: 4, .. }` (weights.rs:24) is not in the match, so GPTQ-Int4 tied models fall to `from_weight_with_scale_inv(embed_weight.clone(), ...)` (loader.rs:1253-1261), i.e. a BF16 lm_head matmul every decode step. The maintainer's own note (LOAD_AND_HISTORY_FINDINGS 'Causa 1') says the gate was meant to cover 'AWQ (e in futuro GPTQ, stesso suffisso)'.
findings.rationale: Per token, the lm_head reads vocab*hidden*2 bytes in BF16. For Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct-GPTQ-Int4 (tie_word_embeddings=true, vocab 151936, hidden 2048) that is 622 MB/token against ~1.4 GB of INT4 body weights, so ~30% of decode bytes; Qwen2.5-1.5B-GPTQ-Int4 is ~37%. The maintainer measured +15-17% decode for the identical mechanism on Qwen3-4B-AWQ (lm_head ~26% of bytes there). Mixed pack layouts in one model are already supported: each PackedQuantLinear carries its own pack_dim (linear.rs:440-457).
findings.proposal: In loader.rs:1241-1242 extend the match to `| Some(QuantScheme::Gptq { bits: 4, .. })`. Keep the comment honest: '4-bit packed schemes (AWQ-4, compressed-tensors INT4, GPTQ-4)'. Optionally make estimate.rs's tied_lm_head_extra_bytes gate on the same scheme set so the pre-load size matches.
findings.expected_benefit: On tied GPTQ-Int4 checkpoints: lm_head bytes/token drop from 2 B to ~0.56 B per weight (4-bit + scales/zeros at g=128), roughly -22% of total decode bytes; expect +15-25% decode tok/s at bandwidth bound, +~175 MB resident. Zero effect on other models.
findings.verify_how: On the M5: load Qwen/Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct-GPTQ-Int4 (or 1.5B) before/after, compare single-stream decode tok/s at temperature 0 and check the top-1 agreement with the ignored `rtn_lm_head_quality_measurement` test pointed at that model's embed_tokens; confirm the log line reports lm_head_extra_bytes > 0.

verdict.reason: Verified in code. The Option A gate at src/models/loader.rs:1236-1243 is `has_packed_quantized_weights && device.is_metal() && matches!(dtype, F16|BF16) && matches!(weights.quant_scheme(), Some(QuantScheme::Awq { bits: 4 }) | Some(QuantScheme::CompressedTensors4))`; `QuantScheme::Gptq { bits, sym }` (src/common/weights.rs:24) is absent, so a tied GPTQ-Int4 model takes `AnyLinear::from_weight_with_scale_inv(embed_weight.clone(), ...)` (loader.rs:1253-1261), a BF16 [vocab, hidden] matmul per decode step. Mixed layouts are fine: `PackedQuantLinear` derives in/out from its own `pack_dim` (src/common/linear.rs:396-437) and dispatches per instance (`(PackDim::Out, _) => w4a16_matmul`, `(PackDim::In, bits) => gptq_matmul`, linear.rs:449-457), and `from_awq` (linear.rs:552-569) builds the PackDim::Out lm_head independently of the body scheme. Nothing in the ROADMAP rejects it; LOAD_AND_HISTORY:56-57 says the gate was meant to cover 'e in futuro GPTQ'; PLAN_COMPARISON:81 measured +15-17% for the identical mechanism on AWQ and CHANGELOG:158 shows 20.4 -> 27.1 tok/s (+33%) on compressed-tensors Qwen3.5-4B when the gate was widened to CT4. The per-token byte arithmetic (622 MB BF16 lm_head on a 151936x2048 model vs ~1.4 GB INT4 body, ~30%) checks out. One correction to the proposal: src/models/estimate.rs:163-172 already adds `tied_lm_head_extra_bytes` for every `is_packed_int_method` (awq|gptq|compressed-tensors) with bits 4|8, i.e. the estimate today OVER-counts tied GPTQ models by the RTN bytes; widening the loader gate brings the two into agreement rather than requiring a new estimate gate. Caveat the maintainer will insist on: no tied GPTQ-Int4 checkpoint appears among the verified models (the GPTQ ones in PLAN_COMPARISON:105-106 are Int8), so this needs verification by execution plus the ignored RTN quality test on that model before shipping. Severity high and effort S stand.

findings.title: rtn_quantize_awq materialises a full F32 copy of the embedding and two extra transposed copies; ~3 GB transient and seconds of load on 250k-vocab models
findings.evidence: awq.rs:676-684 `let w: Vec<f32> = weight.to_device(&Device::Cpu)?.to_dtype(DType::F32)?.flatten_all()?.to_vec1()?;` then 690-692 `let mut qnib = vec![0u8; out_features * in_features]; let mut znib = ...; let mut scl = ...;` (w and qnib coexist until `drop(w)` at 734). Pass 2 (737-752) writes out-major `qw_om: Vec<i32>` [packed_out, in], and 754-765 then do `Tensor::from_vec(qw_om, (packed_out, in_features), &cpu)?.t()?.contiguous()?` and the same for qzeros and scales, i.e. a second full copy of each via candle's single-threaded strided transpose. The maintainer measured this exact path at +5 s on gemma-4-E2B and +0.3-0.4 s on 1-1.5B models when it was mis-gated (LOAD_AND_HISTORY_FINDINGS, Causa 1).
findings.rationale: For Qwen3.5-4B (vocab 248320 x hidden 2560) the F32 copy is 2.54 GB and qnib 0.64 GB, so peak transient host memory is ~3.2 GB on top of the BF16 embedding already resident on the device; the transpose of a 318 MB i32 matrix is a strided single-threaded copy. The work is repeated on every load of the model although the input (embed_tokens) never changes.
findings.proposal: (a) Read the BF16/F16 tensor once (`to_vec1::<half::bf16>()`) and convert per group inside the rayon closure, dropping the F32 materialisation; (b) in pass 2 write directly into the AWQ [in, packed_out] layout by parallelising over `i` chunks (each task reads 8 contiguous qnib rows for its words) so the `.t().contiguous()` copies disappear; (c) optionally persist the triplet next to the checkpoint (e.g. `lm_head.rtn4.safetensors`, keyed by the embed tensor's safetensors offset+size) so warm loads skip RTN entirely, which fits the 'loader perf' item the maintainer already tracks.
findings.expected_benefit: Transient host memory -2.5 GB on 250k-vocab models; RTN time roughly halved (one pass over BF16 instead of cast + two transposes); with (c) the Option A load cost goes to ~0 on repeat loads (the measured +5 s on gemma-class vocab sizes).
findings.verify_how: Time `oxydllm run Qwen3-4B-AWQ` cold vs warm before/after, and watch peak RSS of the loader (`/usr/bin/time -l`). The existing `rtn_quantize_awq_round_trips` test and the ignored quality test must stay bit-identical (RTN is deterministic, so compare the qweight bytes before/after the rewrite).

verdict.reason: Verified (the reviewer's line numbers are ~20 high; the code is at src/common/awq.rs:636-739). The F32 materialisation is at awq.rs:657-662 (`to_device(Cpu).to_dtype(F32).flatten_all().to_vec1()`), `qnib`/`znib`/`scl` at 670-672 coexist with `w` until `drop(w)` at 708, pass 2 writes out-major `qw_om`/`qz_om` (711-727), and all three outputs go through `Tensor::from_vec(..).t()?.contiguous()?` at 730-738, a second full strided copy each. It runs once per load of a tied 4-bit model (loader.rs:1245). The measured cost is real: LOAD_AND_HISTORY:49-54 shows +5 s on gemma-4-E2B and +0.3-0.4 s on 1-1.5B models for exactly this path. Proposal (a) is bit-identical by construction (bf16->f32 per element is exact and the per-group min/max/round sees the same f32 values); (b) writes the same words into the transposed index directly, so `rtn_quantize_awq_round_trips` and the ignored quality test stay byte-identical. (a)+(b) are S. Proposal (c), a sidecar `lm_head.rtn4.safetensors`, is a separate M item with policy questions (writing into the model dir / HF cache, invalidation keyed on file identity) and should not be counted in the S estimate; the ROADMAP's loader-perf item is the right home for it. With (c) left aside the expected benefit is roughly half the measured RTN time plus the 2x-BF16 transient (2.5 GB on a 248k x 2560 embedding).

findings.title: rtn_quantize_awq's geometry bails propagate with `?` and fail the whole load for tied 4-bit models whose vocab is not a multiple of 8 or hidden not a multiple of 128
findings.evidence: awq.rs:663-673: `if out_features % AWQ_PACK_FACTOR != 0 { anyhow::bail!("rtn_quantize_awq: out_features ({out_features}) must be a multiple of {AWQ_PACK_FACTOR}") } if group_size == 0 || in_features % group_size != 0 { anyhow::bail!(...) }`. The caller at loader.rs:1245 is `let raw = crate::common::awq::rtn_quantize_awq(&embed_weight, 128)?;` with the group size hard-coded and the error propagated, so the else-branch (plain BF16 tied head, loader.rs:1253-1261) is never reached. hf_parser.rs:1126-1140's Granite fixture has `vocab_size: 49159, tie_word_embeddings: true` (49159 % 8 == 7). estimate.rs:772-774 handles the same case gracefully (`return None`), so the two disagree.
findings.rationale: A tied, 4-bit AWQ/compressed-tensors (or, after finding 1, GPTQ-4) checkpoint with such a geometry (Granite-3.x 2B with vocab 49155/49159, GPT-2-derived 50257 vocabs, any hidden size like 1792 or 2816) is refused outright with an error about an optimisation the user never asked for, although every other tensor loads fine.
findings.proposal: At the call site wrap it: `match rtn_quantize_awq(&embed_weight, g) { Ok(raw) => ..., Err(e) => { tracing::warn!(%e, "tied lm_head stays BF16"); plain path } }`, and pick `g` as the largest of [128, 64, 32] dividing hidden_size (the W4A16 kernels are already parity-tested at group sizes 32 and 64 per the alpha.12.2 notes). For vocab % 8 != 0, either fall back or pad out_features to a multiple of 8 with zero rows and narrow the logits after the matmul.
findings.expected_benefit: Removes a hard load failure on a supported scheme; tied 4-bit models with odd vocabularies load (and, with padding, still get the Option A speedup).
findings.verify_how: Unit test: build a 16x72 (vocab 72 % 8 == 0 but hidden 72 % 128 != 0) and a 15x128 weight, assert rtn_quantize_awq errors today; after the change assert the loader test harness falls back. E2E: any AWQ Granite-2B community quant on the M5 should load instead of erroring.

verdict.reason: The mechanism is real: awq.rs:643-651 bails on `out_features % 8 != 0` and `in_features % group_size != 0`, the call site loader.rs:1245 is `rtn_quantize_awq(&embed_weight, 128)?` with `?`, so the plain-tied else-branch (1253-1261) is unreachable on that geometry and the whole load fails for an optimisation nobody asked for; estimate.rs:772-774 returns None gracefully on the same geometry, so the two disagree. But the exposure is smaller than claimed: the reviewer's hidden-size examples are wrong (1792 = 14x128 and 2816 = 22x128 both pass), and essentially every transformer hidden size in use is a multiple of 128, so the realistic trigger is only `vocab % 8 != 0` on a tied AWQ-4/CT-4 checkpoint (Granite-3.x 49155/49159, GPT-2-derived 50257), none of which is among the verified models. The group-size fallback and the pad-to-multiple-of-8 variants add risk for no verified case: padding changes the lm_head shape and needs a logits narrow on the decode path, and I could not confirm the W4A16 GEMV at g=32/64 from the code (CHANGELOG:138 documents g=32/64 parity for the staged prefill GEMM only).
verdict.corrected_benefit: Removes a hard load failure with a misleading error on tied 4-bit checkpoints whose vocab is not a multiple of 8; those models load with a BF16 lm_head exactly as 8-bit tied models do today. No effect on any verified model.
verdict.corrected_proposal: At loader.rs:1245 replace `let raw = rtn_quantize_awq(&embed_weight, 128)?;` with a `match`: on `Err(e)` emit `tracing::warn!(%e, "tied lm_head stays BF16")` and fall through to the existing `from_weight_with_scale_inv` branch with `extra = 0`. Keep g = 128 and do not pad. Add a unit test on a 15x128 weight asserting the error, and a loader-level test asserting the fallback.

findings.title: compressed_to_awq converts device-resident tensors: readback, 8x-redundant scattered transposition, serial scales loop, re-upload, once per projection per layer
findings.evidence: The caller `try_get_compressed` (weights.rs:541-553) passes tensors from the map that ModelWeights::load already moved to the device (weights.rs:390-396 `.to_device(device)` for every tensor). awq.rs:195 `let ct = read_packed_to_u32(weight_packed)?;` goes through awq.rs:149-151 `t.to_device(&Device::Cpu)` (a GPU readback). The transposition at 203-217 runs `par_chunks_mut(packed_out)` over output rows i, and for each word reads `ct[o * packed_in + c]` for 8 different o with stride packed_in: every CT word is fetched 8 times (once per nibble position, from up to 8 different rayon tasks). awq.rs:219-224 transposes scales in a serial double loop. awq.rs:229-240 then `Tensor::from_vec(..., &Device::Cpu)?.to_device(device)?` uploads all three again, and `concat_awq_along_out` (243-311) reads the result back once more for q/k/v and gate/up.
findings.rationale: For a Qwen3.5-4B INT4 checkpoint (~2.2 GB packed) that is ~2.2 GB down + 2.2 GB up for conversion plus ~1.4 GB down + 1.4 GB up for fusion, about 7 GB of staged Metal copies that the two-phase loader was specifically designed to avoid, plus the 8x read amplification on the CPU side. The block loop is sequential (loader.rs:1296-1313), so these costs add linearly per layer.
findings.proposal: Move the conversion into the CPU phase of ModelWeights::load: when a tensor named `*.weight_packed` with a sibling `*.weight_scale` is decoded, run compressed_to_awq on the CPU tensors and insert the result under `{prefix}.qweight/.qzeros/.scales`, setting quant_scheme to `Awq { bits: 4 }`; `try_get_compressed` then becomes `try_get_awq`. Independently, restructure the inner loop to `par_chunks_mut(8 * packed_out)` (one task per CT column word c) so each CT word is read once and all 8 nibbles are scattered from registers, and parallelise the scales transpose with the same chunking.
findings.expected_benefit: Removes two of the three bus round trips for compressed-tensors models (the fusion one is finding 5) and ~7/8 of the scattered reads; expect on the order of 1-3 s off a 4B INT4 load on the M5 (bounded by candle's Metal copy throughput), and the conversion overlaps with other CPU decode work in phase 1.
findings.verify_how: Time the load of a compressed-tensors Qwen3.5-4B before/after with `RUST_LOG=info` timestamps around 'Packed-quant attention loader engaged'; `compressed_to_awq_matches_direct_dequant` must still pass bit-exact; run the existing byte-identity E2E on the same model.

verdict.reason: Verified end to end. `ModelWeights::load` moves every tensor to the device in phase 2 (weights.rs:390-396) after an explicitly CPU-only phase 1 (weights.rs:342-355 comment and the rayon `par_iter` at 357-371). `try_get_compressed` (weights.rs:542-553) then hands those device tensors to `compressed_to_awq`, which reads them back (`read_packed_to_u32` at awq.rs:157-160 does `t.to_device(&Device::Cpu)`), rebuilds qweight with a loop (awq.rs:203-217) in which each AWQ row i reads `ct[o * packed_in + c]` for 8 values of o at shift `4*(i%8)`, so every CT word is fetched 8 times from 8 different rayon tasks, transposes scales serially (221-226), and re-uploads all three (`Tensor::from_vec(.., &Device::Cpu)?.to_device(device)?` at 246-252). Fusion then reads the result back once more (`concat_awq_along_out`, awq.rs:281-305, `to_cpu`) and `from_quant` uploads again (linear.rs:578-583). Per projection per layer, sequential block loop (loader.rs:1296-1313). The scales transpose is negligible (KBs per projection), so strike that part; the real costs are the three device round trips (about 6x packed bytes of copies plus one command-buffer sync per `to_device(Cpu)`, roughly 7 projections x layers of them) and ~17 GB of cache-hostile reads on a 2.2 GB checkpoint. On unified memory each copy is memcpy-speed, so the honest bound is 1-3 s as stated, which is a large share of a load that CHANGELOG:148 shows at 1.4-2 s for comparable models. Moving the conversion into phase 1 is implementable: the names `*.weight_packed`/`*.weight_scale` identify the format without the scheme (which is only attached afterwards via `with_quant_scheme`, weights.rs:435), and the result is already `QuantWeight::new_awq(4, ..)` (awq.rs:253), so relabelling to `Awq { bits: 4 }` changes nothing downstream. `compressed_to_awq_matches_direct_dequant` (awq.rs:748-797) pins the bits. Effort M is honest; the loop restructure alone (one task per CT column word, scatter 8 nibbles from registers) is an S first step.

findings.title: AWQ q/k/v and gate/up fusion keeps the unfused packed tensors alive on the device for the whole load: ~65% of packed body bytes doubly resident at peak
findings.evidence: awq.rs:280-287: `// Concatenation must happen on CPU: candle Metal lacks copy2d for I32/U32.` ... `let to_cpu = |t: &Tensor, name: &str| t.to_device(&cpu)`; the parts are `.clone()`d Arc handles from the map (weights.rs:525-527 `self.try_get(...)?.clone()`), and the fused result is uploaded by `AnyLinear::from_quant` (linear.rs:578-583 `raw.to_device(device)`). `weights` is borrowed immutably by every `TransformerBlock::load(&block_cfg, i, &weights)` (loader.rs:1311) and there is no `drop(weights)` anywhere in loader.rs (grep), so the originals stay in `ModelWeights.tensors` until the loader function returns. Call sites: ffn.rs:245 `concat_awq_along_out(&[gate_raw, up_raw])`, attention.rs:378 `concat_awq_along_out(&[q_raw, k_raw, v_raw])`.
findings.rationale: On Qwen3-4B-AWQ (2.48 GB packed) the fused projections are q+k+v (2560x6144) and gate+up (2x2560x9728) = 65.5M of 100.9M packed elements, so ~1.6 GB of duplicate device buffers at peak load, on top of the bus round trip. The manager's eviction decision (manager.rs:488-498) is made from steady-state `runtime_size_bytes`, not this peak, so on a 24 GB machine with another model resident the load can hit Metal OOM or the silent-zeroing failure mode the alpha.13 notes describe, without the accounting predicting it.
findings.proposal: Give ModelWeights a `take_quant(&self, prefix)` built on interior mutability (the map behind a Mutex, or `FxHashMap<String, OnceCell>`-style take) and use it in attention.rs/ffn.rs for projections that are fused, so each layer's originals are released as soon as the fused tensor exists; or, more structurally, decide fusion in the CPU phase (the fusion predicate only needs shapes and bias presence) and upload the fused tensor once, never the parts.
findings.expected_benefit: Peak device memory during load drops from ~1.65x to ~1.0x packed bytes (+ one layer); the fused-upload volume halves. Makes 'load a 4-bit model next to a resident one' predictable on 16-24 GB machines.
findings.verify_how: Log `metal device current allocated bytes` (or Activity Monitor GPU memory) at peak during the load of Qwen3-4B-AWQ before/after; `concat_awq_along_out_matches_separate_dequant` and the 8/8 AWQ byte-identical E2E reruns must hold.

verdict.reason: Verified. The parts are clones of map entries (`self.try_get(..)?.clone()`, weights.rs:524-526), `concat_awq_along_out` moves them to CPU and cats (awq.rs:281-322), and `AnyLinear::from_quant` uploads the fused result as a new buffer (linear.rs:578-583); the call sites are src/common/attention.rs:378 (`concat_awq_along_out(&[q_raw, k_raw, v_raw])`) and src/common/ffn.rs:245 (`&[gate_raw, up_raw]`). `weights` is only ever borrowed (`TransformerBlock::load(&block_cfg, i, &weights)`, loader.rs:1311), there is no `drop(weights)` in loader.rs (grep), and the `ModelWeights` lives until `load_batch_model` returns at loader.rs:1444-1449, so every unfused original stays resident for the entire block loop. The 65% figure checks out for Qwen3-4B-AWQ geometry (q/k/v 2560x6144 plus gate/up 2560x19456 = 65.5M of 100.9M packed elements per layer), i.e. ~1.6 GB of duplicate device buffers at peak on a 2.5 GB model, and the manager's eviction decision (manager.rs:484-498) is computed from steady-state file bytes plus expansion, so the peak is unaccounted. The structural fix is the same one finding 4 wants: in phase 1 the map is a local `mut FxHashMap` (weights.rs:382-386), so deciding fusion there (shapes and `.bias` presence are all in the map) and uploading the fused tensor once removes both the duplicate residency and the CPU readback. The interior-mutability `take_quant` variant is the smaller change. M is honest for either.

findings.title: GPTQ act-order is only detected from a config flag that defaults to false; g_idx is never read, so a mislabelled desc_act checkpoint loads and decodes garbage silently
findings.evidence: hf_parser.rs:876-882: `let desc_act = v["desc_act"].as_bool().unwrap_or(false); if desc_act { anyhow::bail!("GPTQ checkpoint has desc_act=true ...") }`. The loader side `try_get_gptq` (weights.rs:532-537) assembles only `qweight`, `scales`, optional `qzeros`; `g_idx` appears in src only in awq.rs:4's doc comment (grep). `fill_gptq_weight` (awq.rs:555-581) and the resident kernels assume `g = i / group_size`.
findings.rationale: An act-order checkpoint whose config lacks `desc_act` (older auto-gptq exports kept it in quantize_config.json, which nothing here reads: grep 'quantize_config' is empty) or whose flag is stale passes validation; every weight then uses the wrong group's scale/zero for most columns, producing fluent-looking garbage with nothing logged, the exact failure class the alpha.13 Llama-GGUF de-interleave bug had. The check is cheap and the evidence (g_idx) ships in the file.
findings.proposal: In try_get_gptq, if `{prefix}.g_idx` exists, read it once (in_features i32 on CPU) and bail unless `g_idx[i] == i / group_size` for all i; log at layer 0 that act-order was verified absent. In hf_parser, treat a missing `desc_act` as 'unknown, verified from tensors' rather than false, and also read `quantize_config.json` when `quantization_config` is absent so GPTQ files in the older layout produce 'desc_act=true unsupported' instead of 'Tensor not found: ...weight'.
findings.expected_benefit: Turns a silent-garbage path into a load error with a reason; one O(in_features) integer scan per projection at load (microseconds).
findings.verify_how: Unit test in weights.rs: a synthetic GPTQ prefix with a permuted g_idx must be rejected, an identity g_idx accepted; E2E: hand-edit a GPTQ-Int4 config to drop desc_act and confirm the load still succeeds only because g_idx is sequential.

verdict.reason: The code claims are accurate: hf_parser.rs:570-575 is `let desc_act = v["desc_act"].as_bool().unwrap_or(false); if desc_act { bail!(..) }`, `try_get_gptq` (weights.rs:532-537) assembles only qweight/scales/optional qzeros, and `g_idx` appears in src only in awq.rs:4's doc comment and the bail text (grep); CHANGELOG:252 even claims try_get_gptq loads 'optional g_idx', which the code does not do, so the changelog is wrong on this point. `fill_gptq_weight` (awq.rs:560-589) and the kernels assume `g = i / group_size`. But the silent-garbage path is narrower than claimed. The quantize_config.json-only layout the reviewer worries about produces no `quantization_config`, so `validate_quantization_config` returns `Ok(None)` (hf_parser.rs:509-511) and the dense loader fails loudly with 'Tensor not found: ...weight' (weights.rs:506-508), not garbage. transformers' GPTQConfig and GPTQModel always serialise `desc_act`, so the remaining trigger is a hand-edited or exotic config with act-order weights. That is a rarely-taken path, and the proposed check is a cheap guard rather than a fix for a live bug.
verdict.corrected_benefit: Turns a hand-mislabelled act-order GPTQ checkpoint into a load error naming the cause instead of fluent garbage; costs one O(in_features) integer scan per projection at load, done before the device upload so it adds no Metal syncs.
verdict.corrected_proposal: In ModelWeights::load phase 1 (weights.rs:357-371, still on CPU), when `{prefix}.g_idx` is present alongside `{prefix}.qweight`, read it as i32 and bail unless `g_idx[i] == i / group_size` with group_size derived from the scales shape; log once at layer 0 that act-order was verified absent. Drop the g_idx tensors from the map afterwards so they are not uploaded. Fix the CHANGELOG/doc claim that g_idx is loaded. Skip the quantize_config.json reader: that layout already fails loudly.

findings.title: config.json is parsed in three places with opposite text_config precedence (parser: text wins; estimate.rs: root wins), and quantization_config is decoded three times
findings.evidence: hf_parser.rs:49-56: `for (k, val) in text_cfg { root.insert(k.clone(), val.clone()); }` (text_config overrides root; the test `text_config_overrides_root_fields` at 743-770 makes this the contract). estimate.rs:497-503 and 761-770 do `obj.entry(k).or_insert_with(|| v.clone())` for the same merge, so root wins there. quantization_config is read by validate_quantization_config (hf_parser.rs:808-958), parse_quantization_from_json (estimate.rs:447-456) and read_quantization_config (estimate.rs:740-750, consumed by manager.rs:488 for the eviction budget); estimate.rs:439-445 also accepts 'compressed_tensors' (underscore) which the parser rejects as unknown (hf_parser.rs:951-955). The module doc at hf_parser.rs:3-4 claims 'This is the ONLY place in the codebase that knows HF config.json field names'.
findings.rationale: The first multimodal config that carries `vocab_size`/`hidden_size`/`tie_word_embeddings` at both levels (LLaVA-style configs do) makes the loader and the pre-load memory estimate disagree, which feeds the manager's evict-or-refuse decision. Three copies also mean the next quant method lands in one place and not the others, as the underscore alias already shows.
findings.proposal: Export from hf_parser a `pub fn effective_config(path) -> Result<Value>` (read + text_config merge, text wins) and a `pub fn quant_info(&Value) -> Option<QuantInfo>`; make estimate.rs and manager.rs call those and delete the two private merges and two private readers. Add a contract test that estimate's geometry/quant readings equal the parser's on a config with colliding root/text_config fields.
findings.expected_benefit: One source of truth for config semantics; removes a latent estimate/loader divergence that would surface as a wrong eviction decision.
findings.verify_how: Write a config with `vocab_size` at root and a different one under text_config; assert `estimate` and `parse` report the same value after the change (they differ today).

verdict.reason: Verified. `parse` merges with `root.insert(k.clone(), val.clone())` for every text_config key (hf_parser.rs:48-56), so text_config wins, and the test at hf_parser.rs:802 (`text_config_overrides_root_fields`, fixture at 806-818 with root vocab_size 32000 / num_hidden_layers 6 vs text_config 128256 / 24) makes that the contract. estimate.rs:497-503 (`parse_geometry_from_json`) and estimate.rs:761-770 (`tied_lm_head_extra_bytes`) merge with `obj.entry(k).or_insert_with(..)`, so root wins there; on the parser's own fixture the estimate would read 6 layers and a 32000 vocab. quantization_config is decoded three times (hf_parser.rs:508-641, estimate.rs:447-456, estimate.rs:740-750, the last consumed by manager.rs:488 for the eviction budget), estimate.rs:443 accepts `compressed_tensors` which hf_parser.rs:636-640 rejects as unknown, and neither estimate.rs nor manager.rs imports hf_parser (grep), contradicting the module doc at hf_parser.rs:3-4. The divergence is latent today (verified multimodal configs keep geometry under text_config only) but it feeds memory sizing and eviction, which the ROADMAP's D1 section treats as the dangerous class. Severity medium, effort S, and the contract test proposed is the right verification.

findings.title: Parser re-implements Gemma-family defaults by architecture-name lists instead of using ArchDefaults; arch_def.attention_scale is never consulted by the HF path
findings.evidence: hf_parser.rs:132-140: `if attention_scale.is_none() && (arch == "gemma4" || arch == "gemma-4" || arch == "gemma4_text" || arch == "Gemma4ForCausalLM" || arch == "Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration") { attention_scale = Some(1.0); }` and 144-150 the same five-name list for the tie default. arch_defaults.rs:56-61 already defines `pub attention_scale: Option<f64>` with the Gemma 4 rationale and sets it at 310-315 for exactly that name list; gguf_model.rs:505 uses `.or(arch_def.attention_scale)`, hf_parser.rs never references `arch_def.attention_scale` (grep).
findings.rationale: Two copies of the same name list drift independently (a new Gemma 4 alias added to arch_defaults would silently miss the HF path and the model would 'answer with control tokens', the failure the arch_defaults comment describes). Also, because the explicit `query_pre_attn_scalar` branch at 120-121 runs first, a Gemma 4 config that carries that key would override the architecture's fixed scale on the HF path but not on the GGUF path.
findings.proposal: Replace 132-140 with `attention_scale = attention_scale.or(arch_def.attention_scale)` placed before the `query_pre_attn_scalar` read (or after, matching gguf_model's precedence, but decide once); add `tie_word_embeddings_default: bool` to ArchDefaults and use `v["tie_word_embeddings"].as_bool().unwrap_or(arch_def.tie_word_embeddings_default)`.
findings.expected_benefit: Removes two duplicated architecture identity lists; the HF and GGUF front ends apply the same fixed-scale rule.
findings.verify_how: Existing tests `missing_tie_word_embeddings_on_gemma_defaults_to_true`, `explicit_tie_word_embeddings_is_respected_on_gemma`, `a_partial_rotary_factor_per_attention_type_reaches_only_its_layers` must pass unchanged; add an assertion that a Gemma4 config parses to attention_scale == Some(1.0).

findings.title: The IQ CPU decoders are the sole oracle for three Metal kernels but are themselves only checked by a magnitude heuristic; a shared mapping error is invisible to the whole chain
findings.evidence: iq_quant.rs:262-266 (test doc): `Not a proof of the bit mapping, which nothing on this machine can give short of running the model; a wrong mapping tends to show as weights far outside the range a trained matrix has, and that is what this catches.` The assertions at 282-290 are `peak > 1e-4 && peak < 1.0` and `nonzero > v.len() / 2`. metal_ops.rs:7832-7834 (`dense()`) uses these same functions as the reference the `mpp_mv_iq*`/`mpp_gemm_iq*_staged` kernels are compared to.
findings.rationale: A decoder error that preserves magnitude (swapped low/high nibble order, a sign-mask index off by four, scales_h shift by 2*ib vs ib) would pass the heuristic and the kernel parity test both, since the kernel is translated from the same reading of ggml. I re-derived the three loops against ggml's dequantize_row_iq4_nl/iq4_xs/iq3_s and they match, so the risk is low today, but nothing in CI would catch a regression. The fixtures (16 real blocks each, iq_quant.rs:236-239) already exist, so the exact expected output is cheap to add.
findings.proposal: Generate ggml's own f32 output for the 48 fixture blocks once (python `gguf` package: `gguf.quants.dequantize(np.frombuffer(FIXTURE, dtype=np.uint8).reshape(16, -1), GGMLQuantizationType.IQ4_XS)` etc.) and commit them as `iq_fixtures/*.f32` beside the inputs; replace the magnitude test with `assert_eq!` on bits (or <=1 ulp, since ggml computes in f32 the same way). Keep the heuristic test as a sanity check for fixture integrity.
findings.expected_benefit: Bit-exact ground truth for the decoders, which transitively makes the kernel parity tests meaningful; closes the 'shared mistake' blind spot for the only quant family candle cannot cross-check.
findings.verify_how: Run the new test on Linux (no Metal needed); the kernel parity tests on the M5 are unchanged.

verdict.reason: Code claims verified: the only decoder test is the magnitude heuristic at iq_quant.rs:282-290 (`peak > 1e-4 && peak < 1.0`, `nonzero > v.len()/2`), and `dense()` in metal_ops.rs:7829-7836 is the sole reference the `mpp_mv_iq*`/`mpp_gemm_iq*_staged` parity test (metal_ops.rs:7906-7926, including the three fixtures) compares against; grep shows the decoders have no production caller, so they exist only as that oracle. However the CHANGELOG 'Unreleased' entry (lines 7 and 16) records that unsloth UD-Q4_K_M files with 117 IQ4_XS, 7 IQ4_NL and 4 IQ3_S tensors now load and run on these kernels, and the maintainer's verification-by-execution rule plus the 30/30 coherence sweep (line 25) means a shared mapping error would already have surfaced as garbage on a 27B model. The gap is therefore regression insurance on code nobody is expected to edit, not a live risk. The proposal is sound and cheap, with one correction: assert within a small tolerance rather than bit-exact, since ggml's f32 operation order (`d * (ls - 32)` then `* k` versus a folded product) need not match the Rust loop bit for bit.
verdict.corrected_benefit: Ground truth for the three CPU decoders that is checkable off-Metal, closing the shared-mistake blind spot for future edits; no runtime effect.
verdict.corrected_proposal: Generate ggml's f32 output for the 48 fixture blocks once with the python `gguf` package, commit them beside the inputs as `iq_fixtures/*.f32`, and add a test asserting `|got - want| <= 1e-6 * max(1, |want|)` element-wise; keep the heuristic test for fixture integrity.

findings.title: iq_quant is compiled only under cfg(test), so non-Metal builds refuse IQ GGUFs although a correct CPU decoder exists; it also hand-rolls f16->f32 that the `half` dependency already provides
findings.evidence: common/mod.rs:67-68: `#[cfg(test)] pub mod iq_quant;`. iq_quant.rs:108-130 defines a private `fn f16_to_f32(bits: u16) -> f32` with a hand-written subnormal loop, while awq.rs:394,399 already use `half::bf16`/`half::f16` from the same crate. The CHANGELOG 'Unreleased' states: 'Off Metal, and on a GPU that compiles the kernel library but cannot build its pipelines, these files are refused with the reason named.' The decode functions take `&[u8]` and write `&mut [f32]` with no device dependency (iq_quant.rs:136-230).
findings.rationale: The task facts say the CPU path works; for UD-Q4_K_M/XL files it does not, and the missing piece is exactly this module: a load-time dequant of IQ tensors to BF16 dense (the same thing the FP8 path does on CPU per weights.rs) would make those files usable off Metal and on the unverified CUDA path, at the cost of dense memory for those tensors only (117 of the tensors in the cited file).
findings.proposal: Drop the `#[cfg(test)]` on the module, replace `f16_to_f32` with `half::f16::from_bits(bits).to_f32()` (keeping the by-the-book test), and in the GGUF loader's non-Metal branch dequantize IQ tensors to F32 via these functions and cast to the runtime dtype, with a log line naming the memory cost. If that is out of scope, at least move the three `include_bytes!` fixtures and the decoders under one `#[cfg(test)]` block inside the file so the test-only intent is visible at the definition rather than at the module declaration.
findings.expected_benefit: CPU/CUDA builds load IQ-mixed GGUFs (correctness-first, memory-heavy); 25 lines of duplicated float decoding removed.
findings.verify_how: On this Linux box (no Metal) `oxydllm run` the unsloth UD-Q4_K_M file after the change and check coherence; before the change it is refused.

findings.title: dequantize_awq is 4-bit only but is the dispatch target for every PackDim::Out weight, so an AWQ bits=8 checkpoint (which the parser accepts) fails on the CPU/F32 fallback with a misleading shape error
findings.evidence: awq.rs:313-318: `let packed_out = out_features / AWQ_PACK_FACTOR;` (constant 8) and 322-327 `if raw.qweight.dim(1)? != packed_out { bail!("AWQ qweight dim1 ({}) != out_features/8 ...") }`; nibble extraction at 379 and 528 masks `& 0xF`. `dequantize_quant` (awq.rs:583-588) routes `PackDim::Out => dequantize_awq` regardless of `raw.bits`, and `QuantWeight::new_awq` accepts bits 8 (awq.rs:56). hf_parser.rs:834-838 accepts `bits` 4 or 8 for AWQ. The W8A16 Metal parity tests (metal_ops.rs:5141, 5342) do not use dequantize_awq as their reference, so no shared CPU oracle exists for the 8-bit layout.
findings.rationale: `AnyLinear::from_awq`/`from_quant` take the CPU dequant branch whenever the device is not Metal or dtype is not F16/BF16 (linear.rs:566-569, 586-589). An 8-bit AWQ model there errors with a message about out_features/8 that does not mention bits. To my knowledge autoawq's GEMM exporter raises NotImplementedError for w_bit != 4, so real 8-bit AWQ GEMM files are rare, which also means the whole Awq{bits:8} path has probably never seen a real checkpoint.
findings.proposal: Either generalise dequantize_awq to `pack_factor = 32 / bits`, `mask = (1 << bits) - 1`, and an order map that matches what w8a16 expects (and reuse it as the W8 parity reference), or make the parser reject `awq` with bits=8 with 'no verified checkpoint' until one exists. Either way, bail early in dequantize_awq with `bits` in the message.
findings.expected_benefit: Removes a misleading failure and an untested dispatch branch; gives the W8 kernel the same CPU oracle discipline as W4/GPTQ.
findings.verify_how: Construct a QuantWeight::new_awq(8, ...) with qweight [in, out/4] and call dequantize_quant on CPU: today it errors with the out_features/8 message.

findings.title: No 8-bit tied-lm_head quantization: the verified GPTQ-Int8 Qwen3 models read a BF16 lm_head that is ~30% of their per-token bytes while a W8A16 kernel already exists
findings.evidence: awq.rs:655-657 `// RTN 4-bit group-wise AWQ quantization` `pub fn rtn_quantize_awq(weight, group_size)` returns `QuantWeight::new_awq(4, ...)` (776); there is no 8-bit variant. loader.rs:1230-1232 comment: '8-bit AWQ takes the plain-tied path'. metal_ops.rs:2050-2062 exposes `w8a16_matmul` ('W8A16 decode GEMV over the AWQ-layout 8-bit packing') and PackedQuantLinear dispatches `(PackDim::Out, 8) => w8a16_matmul` (linear.rs:449-451). CHANGELOG alpha.12: 'Qwen/Qwen3-{0.6B,1.7B}-GPTQ-Int8 reach 85+ tok/s' (both tie embeddings).
findings.rationale: Qwen3-1.7B-GPTQ-Int8: lm_head BF16 = 151936 x 2048 x 2 B = 622 MB/token versus ~1.4 GB of INT8 body, ~30% of decode bytes; an 8-bit RTN at g=128 halves it (-15% of total bytes) with negligible quality loss (8-bit RTN is near-lossless, so unlike Option A no quality trade-off needs re-measuring). Qwen3-0.6B-GPTQ-Int8 is more extreme (lm_head 311 MB vs ~0.4 GB body).
findings.proposal: Add `rtn_quantize_wn(weight, group_size, bits)` producing the W8 layout the w8a16 kernel consumes (pack factor 4; confirm the order map from quant_kernels.metal's w8a16 reader), reuse pass 1 with max_int = 2^bits - 1, and extend the loader gate with `Gptq { bits: 8, .. } | Awq { bits: 8 }` choosing bits from the scheme. Account the extra bytes in estimate.rs as for 4-bit.
findings.expected_benefit: On tied 8-bit models: ~-15% decode bytes/token, expect +10-15% tok/s on Qwen3-1.7B-GPTQ-Int8 and more on 0.6B; +~320 MB resident on 1.7B.
findings.verify_how: A/B decode tok/s on Qwen3-1.7B-GPTQ-Int8 at temperature 0 with the 10/10 hash-identical rerun check; top-1 agreement via the ignored quality test adapted to bits=8 should be >99%.

verdict.reason: Verified. loader.rs:1230-1232 states '8-bit AWQ takes the plain-tied path' and the gate at 1236-1243 admits only `Awq { bits: 4 }` and `CompressedTensors4`, so tied GPTQ-Int8/AWQ-8 models keep a BF16 lm_head. `rtn_quantize_awq` is 4-bit only (`QuantWeight::new_awq(4, ..)`, awq.rs:739); no 8-bit RTN exists (grep). The consuming kernel exists: `w8a16_matmul` (metal_ops.rs:2050-2060, 'W8A16 decode GEMV over the AWQ-layout 8-bit packing'), dispatched by `(PackDim::Out, 8)` at linear.rs:449-451, with pack factor `32 / bits = 4` (linear.rs:412) and, per quant_kernels.metal:13 and :47 (`return (BITS == 4u) ? AWQ_PACK_ORDER[k] : k;`), a sequential nibble order for 8-bit, so the packer is pass 2 of the existing routine with max_int 255 and no interleave. estimate.rs:163-172 already counts the extra bytes for 8-bit tied models (`awq_qweight_expansion` accepts 4|8), so accounting needs no change. The byte arithmetic is right (622 MB BF16 lm_head vs ~1.4 GB INT8 body on Qwen3-1.7B, ~30%; halving it removes ~15% of bytes/token). One tempering note on the benefit: PLAN_COMPARISON:105-106 measured 42 tok/s on Qwen3-1.7B-GPTQ-Int8, i.e. only ~84 GB/s effective, below the M5's bandwidth, so decode there is not purely bandwidth-bound and the realistic gain is +8-15% rather than the full byte reduction; on 0.6B the lm_head share is larger. Medium / M / 0.6 are honest; verification via the 10/10 hash-identical rerun and an 8-bit variant of the ignored quality test is the right protocol.

findings.title: compressed-tensors validation hardcodes config_groups.group_0 and GPTQ logging prints group_size 128 for per-channel (-1) checkpoints
findings.evidence: hf_parser.rs:911-912: `let groups = v["config_groups"].as_object().map(|g| g.len()).unwrap_or(0); let w = &v["config_groups"]["group_0"]["weights"];` so a single group under any other name yields `num_bits = 0`, `wtype = ''` and the error at 925-931 reports 'got groups=1, bits=0, sym=false, type=''' for a config that is actually int4 symmetric. hf_parser.rs:869 `let group_size = v["group_size"].as_u64();` is None for the JSON value -1, and 894 logs `group_size = group_size.unwrap_or(128)`, so a per-channel GPTQ file logs 'group_size=128'.
findings.rationale: llm-compressor lets recipes name the group (the default is group_0 but recipes commonly use names like 'W4A16'); the user then sees a rejection whose numbers are fabricated by the defaults. The GPTQ log is wrong in the same way for -1. Both are diagnostics, but the compressed-tensors one is a refusal.
findings.proposal: Iterate the single entry of `config_groups` (`as_object().and_then(|g| g.values().next())`) instead of indexing 'group_0'; read `group_size` with `as_i64()` and log 'per-channel' for -1 (and skip the desc_act rejection when group_size == -1, where act-order is a no-op).
findings.expected_benefit: Correct refusal messages and logs; per-channel desc_act GPTQ files become loadable (the runtime path is identical to desc_act=false there).
findings.verify_how: Parser unit tests: a compressed-tensors config whose group is named 'W4A16' parses to CompressedTensors4; a GPTQ config with group_size -1 and desc_act true parses to Gptq.

findings.title: Mxfp4Linear silently falls back to a per-call GPU-readback + dense F32 dequant when activations are not BF16 on Metal
findings.evidence: mxfp4.rs:140-150: `let y_2d = if x.device().is_metal() && x.dtype() == DType::BF16 { super::metal_ops::mxfp4_matmul(...) } else { self.forward_cpu_reference(&x_2d, m)? };` and 170-180 `forward_cpu_reference`: `let blocks = self.blocks.to_vec1::<u8>()?; let scales = self.scales.to_vec1::<u8>()?; let w = dequantize_mxfp4_f32(...)?; let w_t = Tensor::from_vec(w, ..., x_2d.device())?...` i.e. for a Metal-resident expert the packed bytes are read back and a dense F32 weight re-uploaded on every forward. The doc at 167-168 says 'not a serving path'.
findings.rationale: No `--dtype` flag exists today (grep), so the branch is unreachable in production, but any future F16 runtime dtype or a stray F32 activation would turn gpt-oss decode into a ~100x slowdown with no log. A reference path that is reachable from `forward` should either be gated to CPU devices or cast `x` to BF16 and stay on the kernel.
findings.proposal: In forward: if `x.device().is_metal()` and dtype != BF16, cast `x_2d` to BF16 and use the kernel (cast the output back), or `bail!` with a clear message; keep `forward_cpu_reference` only for `Device::Cpu`. Also drop the dead `let _ = m;`.
findings.expected_benefit: Prevents a silent two-orders-of-magnitude regression on the MXFP4 path when the runtime dtype surface changes; no effect today.
findings.verify_how: Unit test on Metal: forward an F16 activation through Mxfp4Linear and assert it either errors or matches the BF16 kernel result within tolerance, and that no `to_vec1` readback occurs (time it).

subsystems.coverage_notes: Read all four scope files in full. Confirmed callers in loader.rs (1195-1345), weights.rs (QuantScheme, try_get_* 470-600, device placement 383-400), linear.rs (PackedQuantLinear/AnyLinear 440-620, Fp8Linear 176-240), ffn.rs (225-275), attention.rs (150-175, 312-410), gdn.rs (375-430), estimate.rs (430-520, 735-800), metal_ops.rs test harness snippets (2050-2062, 5085-5172, 7795-7845), moe.rs (400-445, 755-830), arch_defaults.rs (struct 40-62, gemma4 310-315), common/mod.rs (module gating), main.rs head, CHANGELOG top, ROADMAP rejected/flag-audit/perf sections, LOAD_AND_HISTORY_FINDINGS Option A section. Not read: the Metal kernel sources (w4a16/w8a16/gptq/iq kernels), the full ModelWeights::load two-phase body, estimate.rs beyond the quoted ranges, gguf_header.rs/gguf_weights.rs, expert_stream.rs beyond grep. Could not run cargo or Metal; all cost estimates are argued from shapes and the maintainer's own measured numbers. The claim that autoawq's GEMM exporter is 4-bit-only is from memory of its source, not verified here. I did not verify whether estimate.rs's tied-lm_head extra-bytes accounting is gated by quant method, so the estimate/loader consistency question for GPTQ is noted but not asserted.
missed: The most concrete issue in these files that the reviewer did not raise is the silent CPU-reference cliff in src/common/mxfp4.rs: `Mxfp4Linear::forward` (mxfp4.rs:122-134) takes the fused Metal kernel only when `x.device().is_metal() && x.dtype() == DType::BF16`, and every other case, including a Metal device with F16 activations, falls into `forward_cpu_reference` (mxfp4.rs:146-160), which reads the whole expert matrix back (`self.blocks.to_vec1::<u8>()`), dequantizes it to F32 on the CPU, uploads a transposed dense copy, and matmuls, on every forward of every selected expert (constructed per expert at src/common/moe.rs:421-428). The doc says 'not a serving path' but nothing refuses it, so a GPT-OSS load with a non-BF16 runtime dtype would run orders of magnitude slower and allocate a dense expert per call rather than fail with a reason; a one-line bail (or forcing BF16 for MXFP4 checkpoints in the loader) closes it and fits the maintainer's 'loud failure over silent slowness' pattern. A second, verified mismatch worth a line: src/models/estimate.rs:163-172 adds `tied_lm_head_extra_bytes` for every packed-int method and both bit widths, while the loader (loader.rs:1236-1243) only performs the RTN for AWQ-4/CT-4, so `oxydllm estimate` and the manager's budget currently over-state the resident size of tied GPTQ and AWQ-8 models by vocab*hidden*0.56 B (175-320 MB on Qwen3-class vocabularies) until findings 1 and 12 land.

subsystems.assessment: The Rust side of metal_ops.rs is in good shape on the things that usually go wrong: every kernel argument goes through `set_bytes` (no per-call param buffers anywhere in the 3714 lines), every op encodes onto candle's shared encoder, outputs come from candle's pool, shape/dtype validation is thorough, the deterministic GEMV geometry mirrors named kernel constants, and the TensorOps path has a sane availability/poison model with fallbacks. The biggest remaining lever is not lock or hash overhead (those are ~100-200 ns per dispatch, well under 1% of a decode step even with two engine threads) but dispatch count on the packed-quant decode path: `w4a16_matmul`/`gptq_matmul` zero-fill an F32 accumulator through a blit encoder, run the GEMV, then cast back, so every AWQ/GPTQ linear costs three dispatches and two encoder transitions where the F8 GEMV in the same file already does it in one; the deterministic kernels write `out[o] = sum` and never need the zeros. The second lever is load time: the FFN/FA/quant pipeline caches cache pipelines but not libraries, so the 3934-line quant source is recompiled once per distinct kernel name under a global mutex (the MPP cache next to it gets this right). What is fragile: the tuned FA tiles bypass the threadgroup-memory check and overshoot 32 KB in F32 (production never runs F32 on Metal, but the unit test does), `kv_head_stride` validates nothing about the batch stride the kernels assume, `StagedWeight::bytes()` dereferences `contents()` of a buffer whose storage mode it does not check, and the SDPA full path with mask support is live-looking code that production can no longer reach. The W4A16/GPTQ op pairs are ~450 lines of near-verbatim duplication that already cost double edits once (the alpha.13 determinism change) and will again; `MppQuantMatmul` shows the unified shape. The probes (`sdpa_probe`, `mpp_owned_kernels_available`) are cheap and run during warmup, so first-request latency is already covered except for kernel classes warmup does not touch (the >16-token dequantize fallback when TensorOps is absent), which the library cache fix also removes.

findings.title: Packed-quant decode GEMV costs three dispatches and two encoder switches per linear: zero-filled F32 accumulator plus cast, which the deterministic kernels never need
findings.evidence: metal_ops.rs:2069-2089 `fn wna16_matmul_inner`: `let out = Tensor::zeros((m, out_features), DType::F32, x.device())?; out.inplace_op1(&W4A16Matmul {..})?; out.to_dtype(x.dtype())`; same at 2501-2520 `pub fn gptq_matmul`. Rationale given at 1699-1701: "Written as an InplaceOp1 on the F32 accumulator because the op needs four input tensors and CustomOp3 tops out at three." But the production (deterministic) kernels overwrite rather than accumulate: quant_kernels.metal:3564 `out[o] = sum;`, 3645 `out[m * p.out_features + o] = sum;`. candle-core-0.11.0 metal_backend/device.rs:269-273 `allocate_zeros`: `let mut blit = self.blit_command_encoder()?; blit.fill_buffer(&buffer, (0, buffer.length()), 0);` (a blit encoder cannot coexist with the open compute encoder, so the compute encoder is ended and reopened). In-file precedent that does it right: F8Gemv at 6630-6631 `let output = device.new_buffer(n_out, DType::BF16, "f8_gemv_out")?` as a CustomOp1 with bytes/scales as fields (6569-6575), kernel writes `out[o] = bfloat(sum);` (quant_kernels.metal:3821); and MppQuantMatmul 2867-2873 likewise holds qweight/qzeros/scales as fields in a CustomOp1, contradicting the three-input rationale. Call frequency: linear.rs:447-458 `chunked_batch_gemv` calls these per linear per decode step (m<=8 per call).
findings.rationale: Per decode token each AWQ/GPTQ linear (typically 7 per layer; ~200 per token on a 28-layer model) issues: pool alloc + end compute encoder + blit encoder begin/fill/end + new compute encoder (zeros), the GEMV dispatch, then pool alloc + cast dispatch (to_dtype). Only the GEMV is useful work. The zeros exist for the retired atomic epilogue (`+=` semantics) which production never selects (QUANT_GEMV_ATOMIC is benchmark-only, 1565-1570). Encoder transitions and extra dispatches are CPU encode time (several us each) plus GPU-side serialization points, on a path that is already small-shape and encode-sensitive.
findings.proposal: Rewrite W4A16Matmul and GptqMatmul as `CustomOp1` on `x` holding qweight/qzeros/scales as fields (exactly the F8Gemv/MppQuantMatmul pattern), allocate the output with `device.new_buffer(m*out, x.dtype(), ..)`, and change the deterministic kernels' epilogue from `out[o] = sum` (float) to `out[o] = T(sum)` (bf16/half), as f8_gemv_bf16 already does; rounding is identical to the current F32-then-cast (one round-to-nearest from the F32 sum) so output stays bitwise equal and deterministic. Keep the F32 `Tensor::zeros` + inplace path only behind `quant_gemv_atomic()` for the benchmark, or drop the atomic kernels from the production op entirely.
findings.expected_benefit: Removes ~2 dispatches, 2 encoder transitions and 2 pool allocations per packed-quant linear per token (~400 of each per token on a 28-layer AWQ model). At the measured 35.5 tok/s AWQ (28 ms/step) and a few microseconds per encoder transition/dispatch on the CPU side, this is on the order of 1-4 ms per step, i.e. plausibly 5-10% decode throughput on AWQ/GPTQ/compressed-tensors checkpoints; also removes the per-token F32 [m,out] intermediate.
findings.verify_how: A/B tok/s at temperature 0 on an AWQ and a GPTQ checkpoint (same prompts as the alpha.13 determinism campaign), confirm bitwise-identical outputs; in Instruments Metal System Trace count encoders per decode step before/after (expect ~2x fewer on packed-quant models); the 48-run bitwise determinism test must still pass.

verdict.reason: Verified in code. src/common/metal_ops.rs:2076-2086 (`wna16_matmul_inner`) and 2508-2518 (`gptq_matmul`) do exactly `Tensor::zeros((m,out), F32)` -> `inplace_op1` -> `to_dtype(x.dtype())` per call, and linear.rs:447-466 (`chunked_batch_gemv`) routes every m<=gemv_max_m (16 AWQ / 32 GPTQ, linear.rs:440-445) packed linear through it, so this is per linear per decode step. The zeros really do cost an encoder switch: candle-core-0.11.0 metal_backend/device.rs:269-273 `allocate_zeros` opens a blit encoder, and candle-metal-kernels commands.rs:192-203 `blit_command_encoder` does `if let Some(enc) = state_guard.current_encoder.take() { self.end_encoding(enc) }` before creating the blit encoder; the next `command_encoder()` (commands.rs:160-186) then builds a fresh compute encoder with a new Fence and `wait_for_fence` on every tracked prior output. Two extra consequences the reviewer did not count: the blit and the cast each increment `compute_count` against `DEFAULT_CANDLE_METAL_COMPUTE_PER_BUFFER = 50` (commands.rs:18, 162-166, 194-197), so command buffers are committed ~3x as often per token on packed-quant models.
