The deterministic kernels overwrite (`out[o] = sum;` quant_kernels.metal:3564, 3645) and never need a zeroed accumulator; the atomic variants are the only `atomic_fetch_add` users (quant_kernels.metal:50-108) and metal_ops.rs:1563-1570 documents 'Production never sets this'. The CustomOp1-with-weight-fields pattern already exists in-file (F8Gemv 6568-6575 allocating `device.new_buffer(n_out, DType::BF16, ..)` at 6630, kernel writes `bfloat(sum)` at 3821; MppQuantMatmul 3380-3389 carries qweight/qzeros/scales as fields), which refutes the 'needs four inputs' rationale at 1699-1701. Numerics: one RNE conversion from the same F32 sum, whether done by candle's cast kernel or `bfloat(sum)` in-kernel, so outputs stay bitwise identical and the 48-run determinism test is unaffected. Worth: ~200 packed linears/token on a 28-layer model, each losing 2 encoder transitions (with fence creation/waits), 2 dispatches, 2 pool allocations and 2 command-buffer-slot increments, on a 28 ms step (AWQ 35.5 tok/s, CHANGELOG.md:96) or 13 ms step (GPTQ 74.6 tok/s): a 1-4 ms/step saving is a fair first-principles bound and the GPTQ case gains proportionally more. Not in ROADMAP rejected list; the only ROADMAP item on this path (AWQ q_proj geometry 1.2x gap) is orthogonal. Effort M is honest because both impls, two kernel families' epilogues and the parity tests change; do it jointly with finding 3 so the rewrite happens once.

findings.title: FFN/FA/quant pipeline caches recompile the whole Metal source once per distinct kernel name, under a global mutex
findings.evidence: metal_ops.rs:1596-1625 `get_or_compile_quant_pipeline`: cache keyed `(device.registry_id(), kernel_name)`; on a miss `let lib = device.new_library_with_source(QUANT_METAL_SOURCE, None)` then `lib.get_function(kernel_name, None)` — the Library is a local and is dropped; identical structure at 533-562 (FFN) and 925-955 (FA). quant_kernels.metal is 3934 lines (wc). Distinct names a single packed-quant model hits: up to three M=1 width classes `w4a16_gemv_{,t16_,s16_}bf16` (1814-1826), `w4a16_gemv_batch_bf16` (m>1, warmup prefill of 16 tokens goes through 8-row chunks, linear.rs:459-466), `dequantize_w4_bf16` (1966-1971, only on a >16-token prefill without TensorOps). FP8/MXFP4/sink paths add `cast_f8e4m3_f32`, `f8_block_dequant_bf16`, `f8_gemv_bf16`/`_batch_`, `mxfp4_gemv_batch_bf16`, `mxfp4_mul_mm_bf16`, `sdpa_vector_sink_bf16` (6424, 6518, 6646, 6820, 6901, 7056) all through the same function. Contrast: MPP path caches the compiled Library per device at 2550 `static MPP_LIBRARIES: OnceLock<Mutex<HashMap<u64, Option<Library>>>>` and builds pipelines from it (2655-2697). The mutex `guard` is held across the compile (1602-1621).
findings.rationale: Runtime compilation of a ~4k-line templated Metal source is hundreds of milliseconds cold (the OS shader cache makes repeats cheaper but each still goes through the compiler service and parses the full source). That cost is paid N times per process where N is the number of distinct kernel names, instead of once; and because the compile holds the global cache mutex, a second engine thread that needs any pipeline of the same family stalls for the duration. Kernel classes warmup does not reach (e.g. `dequantize_w4_bf16` on the first long prefill when TensorOps is unavailable) pay a full recompile inside a user request.
findings.proposal: Mirror the MPP design: one `static {FFN,FA,QUANT}_LIBRARIES: OnceLock<Mutex<HashMap<u64, Library>>>` per source (or a single generic `PipelineCache { source: &'static str, libraries, pipelines }` instantiated four times, which also deletes three copies of the compile function), compile the Library once per device, and build pipelines from the cached Library. Optionally pre-build the small set of kernel names a model will use at load (the loader knows bits/dtype/width classes) so no compile ever happens inside a request.
findings.expected_benefit: (N-1) full library compiles saved per process, N≈3-5 for packed-quant, FP8 and MXFP4 models: roughly 0.3-2 s less warmup per model, and no mid-serving recompile stall for a kernel class first reached after warmup.
findings.verify_how: Add a tracing span around `new_library_with_source` and count calls during `oxydllm serve` load + warmup of an AWQ model (expect >=4 today, 1 after); compare load wall-clock; with two models loaded, confirm no cross-model stall on first-use kernels.

verdict.reason: Accurate. metal_ops.rs:1596-1625 (`get_or_compile_quant_pipeline`), 533-562 (`get_or_compile_ffn_pipeline`) and 925-955 (`get_or_compile_fa_pipeline`) are structurally identical: cache keyed `(registry_id, kernel_name)`, on a miss `device.new_library_with_source(SOURCE, None)` with the `Library` dropped at scope end, and the `guard` held across the compile. candle-metal-kernels-0.11.0 metal/device.rs:104-115 shows `new_library_with_source` is a bare `newLibraryWithSource_options_error` call with no caching, so every distinct kernel name re-parses and re-compiles the whole source. The MPP path at 2550 (`MPP_LIBRARIES: OnceLock<Mutex<HashMap<u64, Option<Library>>>>`) and 2655-2697 (`mpp_library(device)` then `lib.get_function`) is the in-file precedent. One correction to the magnitude: `wc -l` gives quant_kernels.metal 3934 lines but ffn_kernels.metal only 242 and flash_attn.metal 604, so the measurable saving is almost entirely in the quant family (3-6 distinct names per packed/FP8/MXFP4 model, W4A16 width classes at 1805-1830 alone give up to 4 of them); the FFN/FA recompiles are cheap and the unification there is mainly for the 3x code deletion. The macOS Metal compiler service also caches source-hash compiles across processes, so the full 0.3-2 s is a first-run-after-build cost and smaller on repeat launches; still real, still inside a user request for any kernel class warmup does not reach. No conflict with ROADMAP rules (system decides; no new flags); effort S is honest for a generic `PipelineCache { source, libraries, pipelines }` used three times.

findings.title: W4A16Matmul/GptqMatmul and DequantizeW4/DequantizeGptqPacked are ~450 lines of near-verbatim duplication, plus 16 copies of the Metal-buffer extraction match
findings.evidence: metal_ops.rs:1711-1930 (`impl InplaceOp1 for W4A16Matmul`) and 2188-2385 (`impl InplaceOp1 for GptqMatmul`) share the same prologue (accumulator dtype check, `x` contiguity and `1..=8` row check, scales dtype check, power-of-two group check), the same `if atomic { 8-name table } else { table }` kernel selection, the same split rule (`chunk = in.div_ceil(s_rows); k_splits = in.div_ceil(chunk)`, GPTQ adds `.div_ceil(pack_factor) * pack_factor`), the same four `match &*sl.0 { candle_core::Storage::Metal(ms) => ms.buffer(), _ => bail }` blocks, identical `set_input_buffer(0..3)/set_output_buffer(4)/set_bytes(5)` binding and the same two-way dispatch. The only structural differences are the packed dimension and the M=1 width-class table (1805-1816). 1935-2030 vs 2386-2500 repeat this for the dequantizers. GptqMatmul 2297 `let s_rows = if m == 1 { QDET_S } else { QDET_S_BATCH };` where both constants are 16 (1579-1580). `grep -c 'Storage::Metal(ms) => ms.buffer()'` = 24 in the file, 16 in scope. MppQuantMatmul 3380-3420 already unifies both layouts behind `crate::common::awq::PackDim`.
findings.rationale: The alpha.13 deterministic-epilogue change had to be applied to both impls and both geometry tables; finding 1 would again touch both. Divergence risk is real (the two impls already differ subtly in how `chunk` is rounded and in which `Params` struct carries `packed_out`), and the parity-test matrix is doubled.
findings.proposal: One `PackedGemv { x, qweight, qzeros, scales, bits, pack_dim: PackDim }` op (CustomOp1 on x, see finding 1) with a `PackedShape` enum wrapping AwqShape/GptqShape that exposes `in_features/out_features/group_size/pack_rounding`, a single kernel-name table keyed `(pack_dim, bits, dtype, class)`, and a `fn metal_buffer<'a>(t: &'a Tensor, what: &str) -> Result<(StorageRef<'a>, &'a Buffer, usize)>` helper replacing the 24 match blocks. Same for the two dequantizers. Delete the dead `QDET_S_BATCH` branch.
findings.expected_benefit: ~400 fewer lines; geometry/epilogue changes made once; buffer-extraction errors impossible to get out of sync; parity tests parametrize over PackDim instead of being duplicated.
findings.verify_how: Existing parity tests (w4a16/w8a16/gptq4/gptq8 GEMV and dequant) and the 48-run bitwise determinism test must pass unchanged; `cargo llvm-lines`/wc confirms the reduction.

verdict.reason: The duplication is real: metal_ops.rs:1730-1760 and 2205-2235 are the same prologue (x contiguity, `(1..=8).contains(&x_dims[0])`, dims2 on qweight/scales, qzeros shape check) with only the packed axis swapped; the kernel-name tables at 1795-1830 and 2280-2295 have the same atomic/deterministic split and M=1 class structure; `grep -c 'Storage::Metal(ms) => ms.buffer()'` is 24 (16 in lines 1-3714); MppQuantMatmul at 3380-3389 already parametrises on `crate::common::awq::PackDim`, so a single `PackedGemv` op is implementable. Two sub-claims do not hold. (a) 'Delete the dead `QDET_S_BATCH` branch' (2297 `let s_rows = if m == 1 { QDET_S } else { QDET_S_BATCH }`): both are 16 today (1579-1580) but they mirror two distinct kernel-side constants (`QDET_S` at quant_kernels.metal:3561, `QDET_S_BATCH` at 3641) that the header comment at 1576-1578 says 'must match'; collapsing the branch couples two kernel geometries and is the kind of hardware-geometry constant the ROADMAP 'Constant and flag audit' section B says to keep. (b) 'the two impls already differ subtly in how chunk is rounded' is not drift: the GPTQ `.div_ceil(pack_factor) * pack_factor` (comment at 2294-2296) is required because the input axis is the packed one. Cheaper path: finding 1 already rewrites both impls as CustomOp1 ops, so the unification should be done inside that rewrite rather than as a separate M-sized refactor; standalone it is a pure maintainability gain with no runtime effect.
verdict.corrected_benefit: ~400 fewer lines and one geometry/epilogue table instead of two, at near-zero incremental cost when folded into the finding-1 rewrite; no runtime change on its own.
verdict.corrected_proposal: Implement finding 1 as one `PackedGemv { x, qweight, qzeros, scales, bits, pack_dim: PackDim }` CustomOp1 (shape handled by a `PackedShape` enum over AwqShape/GptqShape, kernel table keyed `(pack_dim, bits, dtype, class)`), add a `fn metal_buffer<'a>(t:&'a Tensor, what:&str)` helper for the 24 match blocks, and merge the two dequantizers the same way. Keep both `QDET_S` and `QDET_S_BATCH` as mirrored kernel constants; do not delete the branch.

findings.title: Tuned Flash Attention tiles skip the threadgroup-memory limit check; in F32 the MMA layout requests 33-37 KB against a 32 KB device limit
findings.evidence: metal_ops.rs:991-996 `fn fa_tile_sizes(head_dim, dtype_bytes)`: `match head_dim { 64 => return Some((32, 32)), 128 => return Some((16, 32)), 256 => return Some((8, 16)), _ => {} }` returns before `let limit = device_threadgroup_limit();` (1001) and ignores `dtype_bytes`. 1043-1062 `fa_threadgroup_bytes`: fp32 region `(br*d + 2*br + br*bc)*4`, P tile `br*bc*dtype_bytes`, tiles `(br*d + bc*(d + 4/dtype_bytes))*dtype_bytes`. For dtype_bytes=4: d=64 (32,32) = 12544 + 4096 + 16512 = 33152; d=128 (16,32) = 10368 + 2048 + 24704 = 37120; d=256 (8,16) = 8768 + 512 + 24640 = 33920; all above the 32768 fallback/limit at 963-970. 1159-1162 selects `use_mma` when br, bc, d are multiples of 8 (true for all three), 1172 `let tg_bytes = fa_threadgroup_bytes(self.br, self.bc, d, dtype_bytes, use_mma)`, 1190 `encoder.set_threadgroup_memory_length(0, tg_bytes)` with no check against the limit. attention.rs:796 admits F32 into the FA route (`matches!(q.dtype(), DType::F16 | DType::BF16 | DType::F32)`). loader.rs:835-839 and 1495-1499 choose F32 only on CPU, so production Metal runs are BF16; the unit test `flash_attn_f32_d64_prefill_matches_naive` (4696) exercises exactly the over-limit case.
findings.rationale: The computed path exists precisely to keep every tiling within the device's threadgroup memory, but the tuned early-return bypasses it and was evidently measured in 16-bit types. Dynamic threadgroup memory above `maxThreadgroupMemoryLength` is an invalid dispatch; on a release build without API validation the outcome is a failed command buffer or wrong output rather than a clear error. Today this is unreachable in production (Metal is always BF16) but any future F32 attention on Metal, or a tuned-tile change, would hit it silently.
findings.proposal: After the tuned match, keep the tile only if `fa_threadgroup_bytes(br, bc, head_dim, dtype_bytes, true) <= device_threadgroup_limit()`, else fall through to the computed search (F32/d64 then lands on (32,16) = 24896 B); and in `FlashAttnPrefill::metal_fwd` bail with a named error when `tg_bytes > limit` instead of dispatching. Add a unit test asserting every tuned (width, dtype) tiling fits 32 KB.
findings.expected_benefit: Closes a silent invalid-dispatch path; makes the tuned list honest about which dtypes it was measured in. No production perf change (BF16 tiles all fit: 22912, 23808, 21376 B).
findings.verify_how: On the M5 run `MTL_DEBUG_LAYER=1 cargo test flash_attn_f32_d64_prefill_matches_naive` and log `fa_threadgroup_bytes(32,32,64,4,true)` vs `device_threadgroup_limit()`; if the validation layer flags the 33152-byte request, the finding is confirmed; if Metal accepts it, downgrade to a documentation note (the mismatch with the kernel-side formula remains).

verdict.reason: The code reads as claimed: metal_ops.rs:991-996 returns the tuned `(32,32)/(16,32)/(8,16)` before `let limit = device_threadgroup_limit()` at 1001 and never consults `dtype_bytes`; `fa_threadgroup_bytes` at 1043-1062 gives, for dtype_bytes=4, 33152 (d64), 37120 (d128) and 33920 (d256) bytes, all above the 32768 default/fallback at 962-968, while the BF16 figures are 22912/23808/21376; `metal_fwd` computes `tg_bytes` at 1192 and binds it with no limit check, and the production selector at 1506 uses `fa_tile_sizes(head_dim, q.dtype().size_in_bytes())`. However the reachability and severity are overstated. Production Metal attention is BF16 only: src/models/loader.rs:835-839 and 1494-1498 pick `DType::F32` solely for `Device::Cpu`. And the exact over-limit case is already executed, not latent: `flash_attn_f32_d64_prefill_matches_naive` (4695-4712) and the f32 d128 case at 4690 run on any Metal device via `metal_device_or_skip()`, go through `flash_attention_metal_prefill` (4208) and therefore through the tuned tiles; candle's `ensure_completed` (candle-metal-kernels commands.rs:317-335) turns a command-buffer error into a Rust error, and the parity assert at 1e-4 would catch garbage. CHANGELOG 'Unreleased' reports 351 unit tests green on the maintainer's machine, so the evidence in hand says Metal accepts this request on the supported hardware rather than failing silently. What remains is a consistency gap (tuned list measured in 16-bit only, no guard against the device limit) whose cheap fix is still worth taking; it is low severity, not medium.
verdict.corrected_benefit: Makes the tuned-tile list honest about dtype and closes a possible invalid dispatch if a future F32 Metal attention path or a tuned-tile edit crosses the device limit; no production perf change.
verdict.corrected_proposal: In `fa_tile_sizes`, keep a tuned tile only if `fa_threadgroup_bytes(br, bc, head_dim, dtype_bytes, true) <= device_threadgroup_limit()`, else fall through to the computed search; in `FlashAttnPrefill::metal_fwd` bail with a named error when `tg_bytes > device_threadgroup_limit()`; add a unit test iterating the tuned widths x {2,4} bytes against 32 KB. First run `MTL_DEBUG_LAYER=1 cargo test flash_attn_f32_d64_prefill_matches_naive` on the M5 and log `maxThreadgroupMemoryLength` to decide whether the F32 tests are relying on undefined behaviour.

findings.title: kv_head_stride validates head and row strides but not the batch stride the FA kernels assume
findings.evidence: metal_ops.rs:3564-3571 `fn kv_head_stride(layout)`: `if dims.len() != 4 || stride[3] != 1 || stride[2] != dims[3] { return None; } Some(stride[1])`. Kernels address batch as `b * h_kv * kv_head_stride`: mpp_gemm.metal:1151-1153 `device bfloat* kb = k + (size_t(b) * p.h_kv + hkv) * kv_stride;` and flash_attn.metal:134 `const uint k_base = ((batch_idx * p.h_kv) + kv_head) * p.kv_head_stride + kv_start * p.d;`. Nothing checks `stride[0] == dims[1] * stride[1]`. Today attention.rs:806-813 passes one segment at a time (`k_parts[i]`), so B=1 and `b` is always 0.
findings.rationale: A 4-D view whose batch stride is not `h_kv * head_stride` (any future batched prefill over a padded cache, or a gathered view) would be accepted and read the wrong rows for batches > 0 with no error. The check is one comparison and the failure mode is silent.
findings.proposal: In `kv_head_stride`, add `if dims[0] > 1 && stride[0] != dims[1] * stride[1] { return None; }` so the callers' existing "rows a head width apart" bail (1151, 3611) fires; or extend the params with an explicit batch stride if batched prefill is planned.
findings.expected_benefit: Removes a latent silent-corruption path at zero runtime cost.
findings.verify_how: Unit test: build k/v as a B=2 view with a padded batch stride (e.g. narrow on dim 2 of a [2, h_kv, T_total, D] cache where T_total > T), assert the op refuses it today's code accepts it and compare against naive attention.

findings.title: Every custom-op dispatch and every routing decision takes a global Mutex<HashMap> lookup shared by all engine threads
findings.evidence: Per dispatch: 533-545 `get_or_compile_ffn_pipeline` (`cache.lock()`, `guard.get(&(registry_id, kernel_name))`, `p.clone()` = objc retain, dropped after encode), same at 925-937, 1596-1608, 2655-2665. Per MPP op additionally 2573-2612 `mpp_library` locks MPP_LIBRARIES and returns `.clone()` of `Option<Library>` just so 2615-2617 `mpp_gemm_available` can call `.is_some()`; called from every `maybe_mpp_matmul` (2843), `maybe_mpp_quant_matmul` (3545), `maybe_staged_quant_matmul` (3195), `flash_attention_metal_prefill` (1489) and `flash_attention_uses_hardware_path` (1553). Per FA call 1020-1035 `metal_supports_mma` locks another Mutex<HashMap>. Per attention forward 1318-1348 `sdpa_available` -> `sdpa_agrees_with_plain_attention` locks a third (attention.rs:784 calls it inside `forward_batch_optional_rope`). All keys hash a `&'static str` by content (SipHash over the bytes).
findings.rationale: Uncontended this is ~100-200 ns per lookup; with ~10-12 custom ops per layer it is tens of microseconds per decode step (well under 1%), so the cost is modest; but the locks are process-global, so two engine threads decoding different models serialize on them, and the design is more hashing/locking than the information warrants: kernel name, MMA support, SDPA soundness and TensorOps availability are all fixed per (device, model) at load time.
findings.proposal: Resolve once, not per call: (a) make `mpp_gemm_available`/`metal_supports_mma` per-device `OnceLock<bool>`-style flags (an `AtomicBool` plus the registry id) instead of cloning the Library; (b) have each op struct carry an `Arc<ComputePipeline>` resolved when the layer is built (the loader knows bits/dtype/width class), or index pipelines by a small enum into a `static [OnceLock<ComputePipeline>; N]` per device so the hot path is a load, not a hash; (c) cache the attention routing booleans (`sdpa_base_ok`, `metal_fa_base_ok`) in the Attention layer at construction. If the HashMaps stay, switch them to `RwLock` so readers do not serialize.
findings.expected_benefit: Removes ~400 lock/hash/retain-release round trips per decode step and all cross-model serialization on these caches; expected throughput gain under 1% single-model, slightly more with concurrent models.
findings.verify_how: Profile a decode step with `OXYDLLM_PROFILE_DECODE` / Instruments Time Profiler and look for `std::sync::Mutex::lock` + `SipHasher13` under `metal_fwd`; A/B two models decoding concurrently.

findings.title: device_threadgroup_limit() constructs a second candle Metal device (command queue, kernels, residency set) to read one constant
findings.evidence: metal_ops.rs:957-971: `static LIMIT: OnceLock<usize>; *LIMIT.get_or_init(|| { let Ok(device) = candle_core::Device::new_metal(0) else { return 32 * 1024; }; ... metal.device().as_ref().maxThreadgroupMemoryLength() ...})`. Called from `fa_tile_sizes` (1001) for every non-tuned width (96, 80, 512, ...), which runs on the first attention forward (warmup) via `flash_attention_metal_available` (1526-1528), a function that has no device parameter although its caller attention.rs:792 has `device` in scope and `flash_attention_metal_prefill` has `q.device()`.
findings.rationale: `Device::new_metal(0)` builds a full MetalDevice: a new MTLCommandQueue, candle's Kernels (library cache), buffer pools and a residency set, then drops it. It is a one-time cost (tens of ms) and a second Metal device object in a process that is careful about having one; the value is 32 KB on every Apple GPU and is already available through the device every op holds.
findings.proposal: Thread the device through: `fa_tile_sizes(device: &candle_metal_kernels::metal::Device, head_dim, dtype_bytes)` reading `device.as_ref().maxThreadgroupMemoryLength()` and caching per registry id (as `metal_supports_mma` does), and give `flash_attention_metal_available` a `&Device` parameter.
findings.expected_benefit: Avoids creating a second Metal device/command queue at warmup; removes a code path whose fallback (32 KB) silently masks a failed device creation.
findings.verify_how: Log inside the OnceLock init; confirm it no longer calls `Device::new_metal`; Instruments shows one MTLCommandQueue for the process.

findings.title: The IQ-kernel availability probe can poison MPP_RUNTIME_BROKEN and disable TensorOps GEMM/FA for every model in the process
findings.evidence: metal_ops.rs:2627-2648 `mpp_owned_kernels_available` iterates `[Iq4Nl, Iq4Xs, Iq3S]` x {staged, matvec, matvec_batch, gather} and calls `get_or_compile_mpp_pipeline(device, name).is_ok()` for each; 2672-2690 that function sets `MPP_RUNTIME_BROKEN.store(true, ..)` on a missing function or a failed `newComputePipelineStateWithFunction_error`, with the log "TensorOps disabled: pipeline '{kernel_name}' failed to build on this GPU"; 2573-2575 `mpp_library` then returns None forever; 2831-2851 etc. all `maybe_*` gates then decline. gguf_weights.rs:683 calls the probe whenever a GGUF file contains an IQ tensor, before refusing the file.
findings.rationale: The probe's purpose is to refuse one file; its side effect is to turn off the BF16 GEMM, staged K-quant GEMM and TensorOps FlashAttention for all other models for the rest of the process, even when those pipelines build fine. The poison flag is meant for the fallback-capable paths (doc at 2556-2559 says it was seen on virtualized GPUs) and is overloaded here. Only matters on GPUs where the IQ kernels specifically fail to build, hence low.
findings.proposal: Add a `poison: bool` parameter (or a `try_mpp_pipeline` variant) to `get_or_compile_mpp_pipeline`; the probe passes `false` and returns its answer without touching MPP_RUNTIME_BROKEN; keep poisoning for failures raised from `metal_fwd` of ops that have fallbacks.
findings.expected_benefit: A GPU that builds the GEMM/FA kernels but not the IQ ones keeps its fast prefill path; refusal of the IQ file is unchanged.
findings.verify_how: Unit test: temporarily make `gather_kernel` return a nonexistent name, call `mpp_owned_kernels_available` (expect false), then assert `mpp_gemm_available` is still true.

findings.title: StagedWeight::bytes() dereferences buffer.contents() unsafely with no storage-mode check, while candle's pool buffers are StorageModePrivate
findings.evidence: metal_ops.rs:3049-3059 `pub fn bytes(&self) -> Vec<u8> { ... unsafe { std::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping(self.buffer.contents(), out.as_mut_ptr(), len); } out }` with the doc "The buffer is shared storage written once on the host". Constructors do not enforce that: `StagedWeight::new(ms.buffer().clone(), dtype, &dims)` at gguf_weights.rs:535 wraps a candle QTensor's buffer; `of_kind((*buffer).clone(), ..)` at gguf_weights.rs:700 and 493 wraps `md.new_buffer_with_data(..)` buffers. candle-core-0.11.0 metal_backend/device.rs:74-76 `RESOURCE_OPTIONS = StorageModeShared | HazardTrackingModeUntracked` (used by `new_buffer_with_data`, 253-258) but 81-83 `PRIVATE_RESOURCE_OPTIONS = StorageModePrivate | ..` used by `new_buffer` (222) and `new_private_buffer` (242). `contents()` of a private buffer is NULL. Today the only caller is `owned_rows` (gguf_weights.rs:466-470) on `LinearWeight::Owned`, which are always built from `new_buffer_with_data`, so the invariant holds by convention only.
findings.rationale: A public, safe-looking method whose soundness depends on which allocator produced the buffer two modules away; the `new()` constructor explicitly accepts candle-owned buffers. The first refactor that slices a `staged` (candle-held) weight through `owned_rows` segfaults in a memcpy from NULL with no Rust-level diagnostic. Also no GPU sync is performed, which is fine only because the bytes are host-written once.
findings.proposal: Make it `fn bytes(&self) -> Result<Vec<u8>>`: check `self.buffer.contents().is_null()` (or `storageMode() == MTLStorageMode::Shared`) and bail with a message; document the shared-storage requirement on `of_kind`/`new`, and consider making `StagedWeight::new` (the candle-buffer constructor) mark the handle as not host-readable.
findings.expected_benefit: Turns a potential NULL-deref into an error; no runtime cost on the hot path (bytes() is load-time only).
findings.verify_how: Unit test: wrap a `device.new_buffer(..)` (private) in `StagedWeight::of_kind` and call `bytes()`; expect an Err rather than a crash.

findings.title: The SDPA full path (q_seq > 8, mask, do_causal) is unreachable from production and is not covered by sdpa_probe, yet remains in the op and the public contract
findings.evidence: metal_ops.rs:141-147 `supports_sdpa_full = q_seq > 8 && ...` and 234-296 the full-kernel branch with mask buffer/stride handling; 1244-1283 `pub fn sdpa(q, k, v, mask: Option<&Tensor>, do_causal, ..)`. attention.rs:830-835: `let use_seg_sdpa = sdpa_base_ok && self.sinks.is_none() && !use_metal_fa && seg.num_tokens == 1 && ...` and the comment at 780-782 "SDPA 'full' mode (q_seq > 1) corrupts outputs past ~16 tokens, so it stays disabled for prefill regardless of FA availability." `sdpa_probe` (1367-1412) only runs `(1, h, 1, head_dim)` queries, i.e. the vector kernels, so the soundness cache at 1318-1331 says nothing about the full path.
findings.rationale: Ninety lines of live-looking code for a path the maintainer already determined is wrong, exposed through a public signature (`mask`, `do_causal`) that invites reuse, and excluded from the one runtime check that guards the op. Future readers will either trust it or re-debug it.
findings.proposal: Either delete the full branch and the `mask`/`do_causal` parameters (keeping the vector-only contract the probe actually validates), or, if the candle full kernel is to be revisited, gate it behind an explicit opt-in and extend `sdpa_probe` to run a q_seq=32 case so the cache answers for it too.
findings.expected_benefit: Smaller op, honest public contract, probe covers everything callable.
findings.verify_how: grep for `sdpa(` callers passing `Some(mask)` or `do_causal=true` outside tests (expect none); run the attention parity tests after removal.

subsystems.coverage_notes: Read src/common/metal_ops.rs lines 1-3714 in full. The parity-test region (3714-6387) was only spot-checked (FA test cases around 4696-4760, the F32 hardware-path test at 4596); the sdpa_vector_sink, FP8 cast/dequant, f8_gemv and mxfp4 ops that live after line 6387 were read only for F8Gemv (6560-6710) as a precedent, not audited. candle-metal-kernels 0.11 is not present in the registry on this Linux box (only candle-core is), so the exact reuse semantics of `Commands::command_encoder()` and the cost of `registry_id()` are inferred from Metal's one-active-encoder rule and candle-core's `allocate_zeros` (blit encoder) rather than read. I did not verify the kernel-side geometry of the AWQ `t16`/`s16` deterministic variants against the Rust `(det_tgw, s_rows)` table beyond the QDET constants at quant_kernels.metal:3341-3347. The maintainer's notes other than the ROADMAP sections requested (NAN investigation, GGUF performance investigation, load/history findings, plan comparison) were not read. The threadgroup-memory finding (metal-ops-core-4) rests on the 32 KB Apple limit, which I could not observe here; it is framed with a one-minute verification. No cargo commands were run.
missed: The reviewer did not look at what the `1..=8` row cap on the packed GEMV ops (metal_ops.rs:1739-1743 and 2213-2217) does to short prefills. linear.rs:440-445 sends every packed linear with m <= 16 (AWQ) or m <= 32 (GPTQ) to `chunked_batch_gemv` (linear.rs:447-466), which cuts the rows into 8-row chunks, runs a full W4A16Matmul/GptqMatmul per chunk (today 3 dispatches each, see finding 1) and then `Tensor::cat`s the pieces. The batch kernels unpack each weight word once and apply it to at most 8 activation rows (quant_kernels.metal:113-118), so a 32-token GPTQ prompt, which is a typical chat turn after a prefix-cache hit, streams the entire packed weight set through the GPU four times plus a cat copy per linear, instead of once; for a 4-bit 7B-class model that is roughly 3 extra reads of ~3.5 GB per prefill, i.e. tens of milliseconds of TTFT, before the MPP quant GEMM path (MppQuantMatmul, 3380-3389, which dequantizes B per tile and reads weights once) is ever considered, because `MPP_GEMM_MIN_M = 64` (2546) was measured for the BF16 GEMM, not for this quant GEMV-vs-TensorOps crossover. The measure-first fix is a paired bench of `chunked_batch_gemv` against `MppQuantMatmul` for m in 9..=32 on the M5, then lowering the packed-linear MPP threshold to the measured crossover; it touches only the dispatch decision, so decode (m=1) and determinism are unaffected.

subsystems.assessment: The tail of metal_ops.rs is small, readable, and every op validates dtype/contiguity/shape before touching the encoder, which is why the format work (F8 bit-exact dequant chain, MXFP4, sinks) has shipped without numerical surprises. The weakest point is not the kernels' math but ownership and dispatch economics: the owned IQ weights hand candle's Arc<Buffer> straight back to the pool, so the buffer is "free" to candle until the load-end drain, which is exactly the class of silent corruption the alpha.15 notes spent weeks on; this needs a one-line type change and a test. On the GPT-OSS path the engine is launch-bound rather than bandwidth-bound: per token the MoE part issues roughly 192 MXFP4 GEMVs, 192 blit fills (from Tensor::zeros before an inplace op that overwrites every output anyway), and about 1,150 elementwise kernels for the clamped SwiGLU, and the sink attention runs 2,048 threads with runtime-D loops; the README's 14.3 tok/s against a ~30 tok/s bandwidth bound is consistent with that. The F8 GEMV keeps the AWQ/GPTQ deterministic geometry but reads one byte per load across 32 strided rows per simdgroup and decodes each byte with ldexp and two BF16 round trips that are provably identity on the inner step, so a LUT plus a k-major lane layout is the lever there. quant_kernels.metal still carries ~2,400 lines of gguf_* kernels nothing in Rust dispatches, and the quant library is recompiled from source once per kernel name, which costs warmup for no benefit. Twenty-six CustomOp/InplaceOp impls (2,485 lines) share six copy-pasted idioms; a 60-line dispatch helper would remove roughly a third of them and make the next op a 30-line job. The biggest single lever for the maintainer's M5 is fusing the GPT-OSS activation into the MXFP4 GEMV epilogue and dropping the zeros fill; the biggest risk to fix first is the owned-weight buffer ownership.

findings.title: Owned IQ weight buffers drop candle's Arc, leaving them reusable by candle's pool until the load-end drain
findings.evidence: metal_ops.rs:8005-8006 (test, keeps `buffer` alive for the whole check): `let buffer = md.new_buffer_with_data(&bytes).unwrap(); let staged = StagedWeight::of_kind((*buffer).clone(), kind, &[n, k]).unwrap();`. Production does the same but drops the Arc at once: gguf_weights.rs:701-702 `let buffer = md.new_buffer_with_data(&bytes)?; StagedWeight::of_kind((*buffer).clone(), kind, &[n, k]).map(Built::Owned)` and :492-493. StagedWeight (metal_ops.rs:3013-3018) stores `buffer: candle_metal_kernels::metal::Buffer`, not the Arc. candle-core 0.11 device.rs:253-265 `new_buffer_with_data` does `subbuffers.push(new_buffer.clone()); Ok(new_buffer)` so after the caller's Arc drops the pool entry has strong_count 1; device.rs:472-485 `find_available_buffer` returns any `Arc::strong_count(sub) == 1` buffer whose bucket is the smallest >= the requested size, and :294-298 `allocate_buffer` hands it out; device.rs:131-140 `drop_unused_buffers` (run at `wait_until_completed`) evicts it from the pool and the residency set. expert_stream.rs:240-243 shows the maintainer relies on exactly this pool semantics for experts.
findings.rationale: Between `new_buffer_with_data` and the loader's drain (loader.rs:858) every `allocate_buffer` for an op output, `to_dtype`, `contiguous`, RoPE table or zeros during model construction can be served from an owned weight's buffer if no smaller free buffer exists, overwriting IQ4_XS/IQ4_NL/IQ3_S weights silently. After the drain the ObjC retain inside StagedWeight keeps the memory alive, so there is no use-after-free, only a corruption window whose hit rate depends on allocation order. The owned_weights test cannot see it because it holds the Arc. The fingerprint check reads a candle-owned tensor, not an owned one.
findings.proposal: Change `StagedWeight.buffer` to `Arc<candle_metal_kernels::metal::Buffer>` and store the Arc returned by `new_buffer_with_data` (so strong_count stays 2 and candle never reuses or evicts it), or allocate owned weights with `md.device().new_buffer_with_data(...)` directly so they never enter candle's pool. Add a test next to `the_owned_kernels_agree_with_the_cpu_reference`: build an owned weight, drop the Arc, allocate and fill a tensor of a slightly smaller byte size, then re-run the matvec against the CPU reference.
findings.expected_benefit: Removes a silent weight-corruption path on the newly shipped IQ4_XS/IQ4_NL/IQ3_S GGUF route (unsloth UD-* builds). No throughput cost; residency bookkeeping becomes identical to every other weight.
findings.verify_how: On the M5: load an unsloth UD-Q4_K_M, patch `find_available_buffer` with a debug log of the buffer pointer it returns, and compare against the pointers StagedWeight holds; or run the proposed unit test, which fails deterministically on the current code when the fill lands in the dropped-Arc buffer (choose the size so no other free bucket fits).

verdict.reason: Verified and the mechanism is wider than the reviewer wrote. StagedWeight stores a bare `candle_metal_kernels::metal::Buffer` (metal_ops.rs:3013-3018) and gguf_weights.rs:701-702 / 492-493 drop the `Arc<Buffer>` returned by `md.new_buffer_with_data` immediately. candle-core 0.11 device.rs:253-266 pushes that Arc into the SHARED pool `self.buffers` under the exact byte size (no `buf_size` rounding), so after the drop the pool entry has strong_count 1; device.rs:472-485 `find_available_buffer` hands any strong_count==1 member of the smallest bucket >= the request to the caller, and device.rs:294-311 `allocate_buffer` draws from that same shared pool. The reviewer under-counted who allocates there: besides `Tensor::zeros` (mod.rs:2081-2087 -> `with_zeros` -> device.rs:431 `allocate_zeros` -> `allocate_buffer`), every candle op output built with `new_buffer_builder().with_size_for(..)` (mod.rs:131, 195, 251, 364, 423, 553 `to_dtype`, 675 `unary_impl`, 861) goes through device.rs:430 `BufferInit::Size => allocate_buffer`; only this crate's `device.new_buffer(..)` uses the separate `private_buffers` pool (device.rs:198-214). The reviewer also cited the wrong drain: the first `wait_until_completed` (device.rs:170-178 -> `drop_unused_buffers` 131-155) after the GGUF tensor build is gguf_model.rs:675 `drain_metal(device, "the model build")`, not loader.rs:858, so the window is the model build itself. Inside that window the code does run shared-pool allocations on the device: gguf_model.rs:514 `Embedding::from_gguf`, :581 `RMSNorm::from_qtensor`, :595-597 `.dequantize(device)` + `.to_dtype(F32)`, block.rs:336 per-layer norm `qt.dequantize(device)`, attention.rs:453 bias dequant, rope.rs:222-224 `matmul`/`cos`/`sin`/`to_dtype`. A 20 KB norm output allocated when no smaller free buffer exists is served from the smallest owned IQ buffer >= 20 KB and overwrites its first rows; the drain then never evicts that buffer (the norm holds the Arc) and `weights_read_consistently` (loader.rs:917-928) fingerprints `self.norm` (gguf_model.rs:703-705), i.e. the tensor that moved in, not the weight under it. Proposal is sound and small: hold the `Arc<Buffer>` (strong_count stays 2, never reused, never evicted from the residency set); the candle-QTensor `StagedWeight::new` path is already safe because the QTensor keeps its Arc. The owned-weights test (8005-8006) holds the Arc for the whole check, which is why it cannot see this.

findings.title: mxfp4_matmul zero-fills its output with a blit before an inplace kernel that writes every element
findings.evidence: metal_ops.rs:6943-6953 `if m <= GGUF_BATCH_MAX { let out = Tensor::zeros((m, n), DType::BF16, x.device())?; out.inplace_op1(&Mxfp4Matmul { ... })?; return Ok(out); }`. candle-core 0.11 device.rs:269-273 `allocate_zeros`: `let mut blit = self.blit_command_encoder()?; blit.fill_buffer(&buffer, (0, buffer.length()), 0);`. The kernel writes all outputs: quant_kernels.metal:3171-3177 `for (uint row...) for (uint m = 0; m < M; ++m) { const float tot = simd_sum(sumf[row][m]); if (tiisg == 0 && r < N) out[(ulong)m * (ulong)N + r] = (bfloat)tot; }` with grid `n.div_ceil(8)` TGs (metal_ops.rs:6829-6840) covering every r < N. The sibling Mxfp4MulMM path already uses `device.new_buffer(out_elems, DType::BF16, "mxfp4-mul-mm")` (6893) with no fill.
findings.rationale: Per decode token on gpt-oss-20b (24 layers x top-4 x gate_up+down, moe.rs:157-172 and dispatch_naive 577-581) this is 192 blit fills and 384 compute/blit encoder transitions, each a GPU pipeline boundary plus CPU encoder setup, purely to initialise memory the kernel overwrites. The AWQ/GPTQ inplace ops need zeros only for their `_atomic` variants; MXFP4 has none.
findings.proposal: Make Mxfp4Matmul a `CustomOp1` over `x` with `device.new_buffer(m * n, DType::BF16, "mxfp4-gemv")` as the output, mirroring Mxfp4MulMM at 6893-6925, and delete the `Tensor::zeros` branch (the struct no longer needs the `x: Tensor` field or the `m` field; `m` comes from `x_l.dims()`).
findings.expected_benefit: Removes 192 blits and 384 encoder boundaries per gpt-oss-20b token; at 70 ms/token (README 14.3 tok/s) and ~20-40 us per encoder boundary this is on the order of 4-8 ms, i.e. roughly 5-10% decode throughput on gpt-oss, plus one fewer pool churn per expert call.
findings.verify_how: Metal System Trace / `OXYDLLM_PROFILE_DECODE` on gpt-oss-20b: count blit encoders per token before (expect ~192 labelled "zeros") and after (0); A/B tok/s on the same prompt at temperature 0 (output must be bitwise identical since the kernel is unchanged).

verdict.reason: Code does what is claimed: metal_ops.rs:6943-6953 `Tensor::zeros((m, n), BF16)` then `inplace_op1`; candle mod.rs:2081-2087 `zeros_impl` -> `with_zeros` -> device.rs:269-273 `allocate_zeros` opens a blit encoder and `fill_buffer`s the whole buffer, then the compute encoder must be re-opened for the kernel. The kernel writes every output: grid `n.div_ceil(8)` TGs x 2 simdgroups x GGUF_N_DST=4 rows (6829-6840, metal:3129-3130) and the epilogue at metal:3171-3177 writes `out[m*N + r]` for every `r < N`, `m < M`, so the fill is dead work. Frequency verified: `MoeExpert::GptOss` calls `gate_up.forward` and `down.forward` (moe.rs:157, 171) once per expert call, `dispatch_naive` (moe.rs:577-580) runs each routed expert, so 24 x 4 x 2 = 192 fills + 384 encoder transitions per gpt-oss-20b decode token. Also note the zeros buffer comes from candle's shared pool while every other op output in this file uses `device.new_buffer` (private pool), so the fix also stops churning the shared pool. The 5-10% figure is an upper-bound argument (depends on the per-encoder-boundary cost on the M5), but the change is S, output-bitwise-identical (kernel untouched), and mirrors Mxfp4MulMM at 6893. Use `apply_op1_no_bwd` as the siblings do.

findings.title: GPT-OSS clamped SwiGLU could be fused into the MXFP4 GEMV epilogue (gate/up pairs already land in one simdgroup)
findings.evidence: moe.rs:157-172 after `gate_up.forward(x)`: `reshape`, `narrow` x2, `squeeze` x2, `clamp` x2, `affine`, `neg`, `exp`, `affine`, `recip`, two `mul`, one `affine` — about 12 elementwise kernels plus views per expert call, then `down.forward(&h)`. The gate/up interleave is along N (`dims.push(2)` then `narrow(D::Minus1, 0/1, 1)`), i.e. output rows 2i (gate) and 2i+1 (up). In the kernel, quant_kernels.metal:3129-3130 `first_row = (r0 * GGUF_N_SIMDGROUP + sgitg) * GGUF_N_DST` with `GGUF_N_DST 4` (:692): rows 4j..4j+3 are always in the same simdgroup, so both members of each pair are available at the epilogue (:3171-3177) in registers (`sumf[row][m]`). The Rust op (6738-6846) already carries `k, n, m`; a `limit: Option<f32>` is all the fusion needs on this side.
findings.rationale: Per gpt-oss-20b token: 24 layers x 4 experts x ~12 kernels = ~1,150 elementwise launches, each with its own output allocation and ~5-10 us floor, plus the `[m, 2*inter]` BF16 intermediate written and re-read three times. The engine is already launch-bound on this model (14.3 tok/s vs a ~30 tok/s byte bound for ~3.5 GB/token), so launch count is the lever. ROADMAP lists MoE decode tuning in the perf backlog and nothing rejects fusion.
findings.proposal: Add a function-constant variant `mxfp4_gemv_batch_swiglu_bf16` (same body; epilogue: for even row r=2i compute g=min(gate,limit), u=clamp(up,-limit,limit), h=(u+1)*g*sigmoid(1.702*g) from `sumf[row][m]` and `sumf[row+1][m]`, write `out[m*(N/2)+i]`) and a `Mxfp4Matmul { fused_swiglu_limit: Option<f32> }` field; in `MoeExpert::GptOss` call `mxfp4_matmul_swiglu` when m <= GGUF_BATCH_MAX. Keep the unfused path for the mul_mm branch.
findings.expected_benefit: Eliminates ~1,150 kernel launches and ~190 intermediate tensors per token on gpt-oss; combined with finding 2 this is the bulk of the per-expert overhead. Rough bound: if each avoided launch costs 5 us of CPU encode + GPU gap, that is ~6 ms of a 70 ms token (~8%); the maintainer's measured per-launch cost on the M5 decides the exact figure.
findings.verify_how: Parity: extend `mxfp4_matmul_matches_reference` with the fused variant against the moe.rs formula on CPU (tol as today). Perf: A/B gpt-oss-20b decode tok/s and Metal trace kernel count per token (expect ~1,150 fewer).

verdict.reason: Verified. moe.rs:157-172: `gu.reshape([.., inter, 2])`, `narrow(D::Minus1, 0/1, 1)` so gate = output column 2i and up = 2i+1 (interleaved along N); then `clamp` x2, `affine`, `neg`, `exp`, `affine`, `recip`, `mul`, `affine`, `mul`. candle's scalar `clamp` is `maximum(min).minimum(max)` with a scalar tensor materialised per call, so the real count is >= 12 launches plus small uploads per expert call; at 96 expert calls per gpt-oss-20b token that is >= 1,150 launches, each allocating an output. In the kernel, `first_row = (r0 * GGUF_N_SIMDGROUP + sgitg) * GGUF_N_DST` (metal:3129-3130, GGUF_N_DST=4 at :692) keeps rows 4j..4j+3 in one simdgroup, so both members of each (2i, 2i+1) pair are in `sumf[row][m]` at the epilogue (:3166-3177); the Rust op already threads k/n/m (6738-6744). ROADMAP lists MoE decode tuning as backlog and rejects nothing here. One honesty note the reviewer omitted: the fused epilogue consumes F32 sums instead of BF16-rounded gate/up, so outputs differ from today's path at BF16 rounding level (still deterministic); the parity test must compare against the moe.rs formula with the mxfp4 tolerance, not bit-for-bit. Effort M is fair (new function-constant kernel variant, pipeline cache key extension, parity test).

findings.title: sdpa_vector_sink runs one 32-thread simdgroup per head with runtime-D register arrays and scalar loads; it will dominate long-context GPT-OSS decode
findings.evidence: metal_ops.rs:7060-7071 dispatch `MTLSize { width: h, ... }, MTLSize { width: 32, ... }` — one simdgroup per query head, no split over kv positions; 7011-7013 bail on `qd[0] != 1 || qd[2] != 1` so each sequence in a decode batch is its own dispatch (attention.rs:895-905 calls it per segment). quant_kernels.metal:3278-3301: `float acc[SDPA_SINK_MAX_D]; for (uint d = 0; d < D; ++d) acc[d] = 0.0f; for (uint j = tiisg; j < p.kv_len; j += 32) { ... for (uint d = 0; d < D; ++d) s += q_s[d] * (float)kj[d]; ... for (uint d = 0; d < D; ++d) acc[d] = acc[d] * corr + w * (float)vj[d]; }` with `D = p.head_dim` a runtime value (3272) and `kj`/`vj` read as scalar `bfloat`.
findings.rationale: gpt-oss has H=64, KVH=8, D=64: 64 TGs x 32 threads = 2,048 threads for the whole attention of a layer. Each lane walks its own 128-byte K row then V row with 2-byte loads, so a simdgroup touches 32 cache lines per load instruction and has almost no memory-level parallelism. `acc[128]` indexed by a runtime bound is likely demoted to thread-private memory. K+V traffic is KVH*L*D*4 bytes per layer: 16 MB at L=8k, 400 MB per token across 24 layers; at the ~10-30 GB/s this geometry plausibly achieves that is 13-40 ms per token at 8k context, against a 70 ms token today. Prefill with sinks also bypasses FA (`use_metal_fa` requires `sinks.is_none()`, attention.rs:810), so decode is the only fast sink path and it is the slow one.
findings.proposal: Rewrite with D as a function constant (64 and 128 instantiations), lanes split along D with `bfloat4` loads and `simd_sum` for the dot (candle's sdpa_vector layout), 4-8 simdgroups per TG each owning a kv-position range with a threadgroup online-softmax combine (sink folded once at the end), and a grid of B*H threadgroups so a decode batch is one dispatch; lift the `qd[0] != 1` restriction in metal_fwd accordingly.
findings.expected_benefit: At L >= 4k on gpt-oss this is likely the largest single per-token kernel; a bandwidth-shaped kernel should bring the attention part to ~2-4 ms per token at 8k (K/V bytes / ~120 GB/s), i.e. a 10-30% decode gain at long context and more at 32k. Also one dispatch per layer instead of one per sequence under batching.
findings.verify_how: Add the sink op to a `wide_head_attention_probe`-style ignored test at H=64,KVH=8,D=64, L in {1k, 8k, 32k}; print GB/s = KVH*L*D*4 / time, and compare with `metal_ops::sdpa` at the same shapes. Then A/B gpt-oss-20b decode tok/s with an 8k-token prompt.

verdict.reason: The kernel is as described: one 32-thread TG per query head (metal_ops.rs:7060-7071), per-sequence dispatch enforced by `qd[0] != 1 || qd[2] != 1` (7011-7013) and the per-segment call at attention.rs:896-905; runtime `D = p.head_dim` (metal:3272), `float acc[SDPA_SINK_MAX_D]` zeroed and updated under a runtime bound (3281-3298), scalar `bfloat` loads of `kj[d]`/`vj[d]` with lane j striding kv positions (3286-3297). Two corrections shrink the estimate: (1) gpt-oss alternates sliding-window and full layers and the GGUF allocator is built `.with_sliding_window(layer_windows[i])` (gguf_model.rs:661) with `truncate_kv_window` narrowing to the window (attention.rs:125), so only ~12 of 24 layers see the full L: ~200 MB/token at 8k, not 400 MB. (2) The same call site currently pays a bigger, cheaper-to-fix cost before the kernel even runs: attention.rs:897-899 `k_seg.contiguous()` / `v_seg.contiguous()` copy the whole K and V every step (see `missed`). The kernel rewrite is still the right long-context fix, but it should land after that stride fix so the A/B measures the kernel alone.
verdict.corrected_benefit: At L >= 8k on gpt-oss roughly half the reviewer's figure (~100-200 MB of K/V per token across the full-attention layers moved at a bandwidth-shaped rate instead of a latency-shaped one), negligible below ~2k context; one dispatch per layer instead of per sequence under batching.
verdict.corrected_proposal: First add a `kv_head_stride` to SdpaSinkParams and accept `straight_in` K/V (see missed). Then rewrite with D as a function constant (64/128), lanes along D with vector loads and `simd_sum` dots, 4-8 simdgroups per TG splitting kv positions with a threadgroup online-softmax merge (sink folded once), grid B*H, and lift the `qd[0] != 1` restriction.

findings.title: F8 GEMV geometry reads one weight byte per load across 32 strided rows and decodes each byte with ldexp plus a provably-identity BF16 round trip
findings.evidence: metal_ops.rs:6654-6666 dispatch `MTLSize { width: self.out_features.div_ceil(QDET_TGW) }, MTLSize { width: QDET_TGW, height: QDET_S }` (32x16 = 512 threads; QDET_TGW=32, QDET_S=16 at 1578-1579). quant_kernels.metal:3795-3807: `uint o = tgid.x * QDET_TGW + tid.x; ... device const uchar* wrow = w + ulong(o) * p.in_features; ... for (; i < blk_end; ++i) acc += float(x[i]) * f8_weight_value(wrow[i], sc);` — a simdgroup is 32 consecutive `o` at the same `i`, so each load instruction touches 32 lines `in_features` bytes apart. :3769-3783 `f8_weight_value`: branches, `ldexp`, then `return float(bfloat(float(bfloat(val)) * sc));`. Batched variant :3828-3850: `float acc[8]` indexed by runtime `p.m`, and `acc[r] += float(x[ulong(r) * p.in_features + i]) * wv;` — 8 scalar x loads per weight byte.
findings.rationale: Every E4M3 value (3-bit mantissa) is exactly representable in BF16 (7-bit mantissa), so `float(bfloat(val))` equals `val` for all 256 codes including NaN sign; the inner rounding can be dropped bit-for-bit. The row-per-lane layout means ~1 load instruction and ~12 ALU ops per weight byte with poor coalescing, whereas the MXFP4 kernel in the same file (:3114-3178) uses the llama.cpp layout (4 rows per simdgroup, lanes along k, 16-byte blocks) and the ROADMAP perf backlog already notes a ~1.2x gap for this exact QDET geometry on AWQ. For a 14.7 MB F8 expert projection (e.g. [2048, 7168]) the current kernel issues 14.7 M byte loads; a k-major `uchar4`/`uint` layout issues 3.7 M coalesced ones.
findings.proposal: (a) Add `constant float F8E4M3_LUT[256]` and define `f8_weight_value(v, sc) = bfloat(F8E4M3_LUT[v] * sc)`; use the same LUT in `f8_block_dequant_bf16` and `cast_f8e4m3_f32` (bit-identical by the argument above; keep the existing test that proves byte-for-byte parity with the CPU chain). (b) Re-geometry f8_gemv(_batch) like `mxfp4_gemv_batch_bf16`: one simdgroup per 4 output rows, lane `il` owns 4-16 contiguous k bytes per block-of-128 (`block_c`), scale fetched once per block, fixed-order `simd_sum` (still deterministic), `m` as a function constant so `acc[m]` stays in registers.
findings.expected_benefit: (a) alone removes ~8 ALU ops per weight byte with zero numerical change. (b) is the bandwidth fix for hot-cache FP8 MoE decode (the README notes hot-cache streaming matches resident speed, so this kernel is on the critical path once experts are cached); plausible 1.5-3x on the expert GEMV itself, which is the dominant byte mover on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8.
findings.verify_how: Add f8_gemv at [2048,7168] and [7168,2048] to `quantized_matvec_bandwidth_probe` and print GB/s next to candle's Q8_0 matvec (same ~1 B/elem); a healthy kernel sits within ~1.3x of Q8_0. For (a), rerun the existing F8 parity tests; they must stay bit-identical.

verdict.reason: Accurate on the code: dispatch `out.div_ceil(QDET_TGW)` x (QDET_TGW=32, QDET_S=16) (6654-6666, 1578-1579); metal:3795-3807 lane `o` walks its own row `w + o*in_features` one byte per iteration so a simdgroup's load touches 32 lines `in_features` apart; `f8_weight_value` (3769-3783) branches, `ldexp`s and does `float(bfloat(float(bfloat(val)) * sc))`; the batch variant (3828-3850) indexes `acc[8]` by runtime `p.m` and issues `p.m` scalar x loads per weight byte. The identity argument for (a) is correct: every E4M3 code (3-bit mantissa, 2^-9..448) is exactly representable in BF16, so the inner `bfloat(val)` round is a no-op and `bfloat(LUT[v] * sc)` is bit-identical. Benefit is overstated: the ROADMAP's measured gap for this exact QDET geometry on AWQ is ~1.2x at the micro-bench, not 1.5-3x, and this kernel only runs for streamed FP8 experts (Fp8Cached, moe.rs:107-113), where a miss is SSD-bound; it matters in the hot-cache steady state only. (a) alone is a pure ALU saving that is neutral if the kernel is already bandwidth-bound.
verdict.corrected_benefit: (a) bit-identical, zero risk, likely neutral-to-small. (b) ~1.2-1.5x on the F8 expert GEMV in the hot-cache regime (bounded by the ROADMAP's measured QDET gap on AWQ), i.e. a few ms per token on a 35B-A3B FP8 decode; nothing on misses.
verdict.corrected_proposal: Do (a) as a one-hour change with the existing bit-parity tests. For (b) copy the mxfp4_gemv_batch_bf16 geometry (4 rows per simdgroup, lanes along k, one scale fetch per 128-wide block, fixed-order simd_sum, m as a function constant) and measure it in `quantized_matvec_bandwidth_probe` against candle Q8_0 before adopting; keep the old kernel until the probe shows the gap closed.

findings.title: The 146 KB quant library is recompiled from source once per kernel name, and ~2,400 lines of it are gguf_* kernels nothing in Rust dispatches
findings.evidence: In scope: 6646 `let pipeline = get_or_compile_quant_pipeline(device.device(), kernel_name)?;` (also 6423, 6517, 6822, 6901, 7051). metal_ops.rs:1596-1623: on a cache miss `let lib = device.new_library_with_source(QUANT_METAL_SOURCE, None)...; let func = lib.get_function(kernel_name, None)` — the Library is a local and is rebuilt for every distinct `kernel_name`; only MPP caches libraries (`MPP_LIBRARIES` at 2550). quant_kernels.metal is 3934 lines / 146,558 bytes; lines 734-2177 define `gguf_q{4_0,4_1,5_0,5_1,8_0,2k,3k,4k,5k,6k}_gemv(_batch)_bf16` and 2644-3058 the matching `*_mul_mm_bf16`. `grep -rnE 'gguf_q[0-9a-z_]+_(gemv|mul_mm)' src --include=*.rs` returns 0 hits; GGUF decode goes through candle `QMatMul` (linear.rs:263-291) and `maybe_mpp_quant_matmul`/`mpp_owned_matmul` (linear.rs:331, 486). In scope, `GGUF_BATCH_MAX` (6387), `GgufBatchParams` (6392), `GgufMatmulParams` (6714) and `GGUF_MM_BM/BN` (6705-6708) are now used only by the MXFP4 ops.
findings.rationale: A gpt-oss run compiles the full 146 KB source three times (mxfp4 gemv, mxfp4 mul_mm, sink); an AWQ run with batched decode and dequant four or five times; each compile parses 2,400 dead lines. Apple's shader cache shortens repeats but each `newLibraryWithSource` is still a synchronous XPC round trip on the engine thread at first use, i.e. on the first request's TTFT after load unless warmup happens to hit every kernel. The dead kernels also mislead readers (the ROADMAP still says `quant_kernels.metal` "implements ten GGUF quantizations").
findings.proposal: Cache `Library` per device in `get_or_compile_quant_pipeline` (same shape as MPP_LIBRARIES: `OnceLock<Mutex<HashMap<u64, Library>>>`), apply the same to FFN (549) and FA (941). Delete the unreferenced `gguf_*` kernels and `GGUF_LEGACY_GEMV_BATCH` from quant_kernels.metal (git keeps them), and rename `GGUF_BATCH_MAX`/`GgufBatchParams`/`GgufMatmulParams`/`GGUF_MM_*` to `MXFP4_*`/`DecodeGemvParams` so the remaining users read truthfully.
findings.expected_benefit: Warmup / first-token latency: N-1 full library compiles removed per model type and each remaining compile over ~40% less source; maintainability: ~2,400 lines of dead Metal removed from a file the maintainer must keep in their head when editing shared defines.
findings.verify_how: Time `get_or_compile_quant_pipeline` on the first call of each kernel (instrument with `Instant`) on a cold shader cache (`rm -rf ~/Library/Caches/com.apple.metal` or a fresh user) before and after; confirm `cargo test` still green with the gguf_* kernels deleted (nothing references them).

verdict.reason: Verified. `get_or_compile_quant_pipeline` (1596-1623) caches only the pipeline keyed `(registry_id, kernel_name)` (1587) and on every miss calls `device.new_library_with_source(QUANT_METAL_SOURCE, None)` (1611-1613) with the Library as a local; the FFN (549-551) and FA (941-943) caches do the same, while MPP keeps `MPP_LIBRARIES` (2550). `QUANT_METAL_SOURCE` is `include_str!("quant_kernels.metal")` (1561). `grep -rnE 'gguf_q[0-9a-z_]+_(gemv|mul_mm)'` and `"gguf_` / `gguf_{` over src/**/*.rs return nothing, so the kernels at metal:734..3058 (26 `kernel void gguf_*` plus the `GGUF_LEGACY_GEMV_BATCH` macro at 1041-1095) are unreachable; GGUF decode goes through candle `QMatMul` (linear.rs:280-291) and `mpp_owned_matmul`/`maybe_mpp_quant_matmul` (linear.rs:331, 486). `GGUF_BATCH_MAX`, `GgufBatchParams`, `GgufMatmulParams`, `GGUF_MM_BM/BN` have no references outside 6387-7112, i.e. only the MXFP4 ops use them. Two notes: the ROADMAP constant audit names `GGUF_BATCH_MAX` and `GGUF_MM_BM/BN`, so the rename should touch that note; and warmup (manager.rs ~900-945) absorbs first-use compiles, so the user-visible cost is load/warmup time, not TTFT. S effort, measurable with a cold shader cache.

findings.title: 26 CustomOp/InplaceOp impls repeat six dispatch idioms; a small helper would remove roughly a third of 2,485 impl lines
findings.evidence: File-wide: 26 `impl (CustomOp[123]|InplaceOp[123]) for` blocks totalling 2,485 lines (Sdpa 233, W4A16Matmul 221, GptqMatmul 195 ... CastF8E4M3ToF32 48). Repeated idioms counted by grep: `Storage::Metal(ms) => ms.buffer()` x24 with a paired `must be Metal-resident` bail x24 (in scope 6631-6639, 6797-6810, 6887-6898, 7043-7046), `storage_and_layout()` x25, `command_encoder()?` + `encoder.as_ref()` x26, `set_compute_pipeline_state` x22, `dispatch_thread_groups` x20 each with two 5-line `MTLSize { width, height, depth }` literals, `MetalStorage::new(` x23, and 26 `cpu_fwd` stubs that only `bail!("... is Metal-only")`. Within the 726-line scope these patterns alone account for 115 lines of the 507 impl lines.
findings.rationale: Every new format (the IQ family, F8, MXFP4, sinks were all added this way) copies 50-100 lines whose only variation is buffer index, byte offset multiplier and grid shape. The byte-offset multiplier is hand-written per call (`* 2`, `* 4`, `* DType::F32.size_in_bytes()`, or nothing for U8), which is exactly the kind of thing that goes wrong on the next copy (F8Gemv at 6650-6652 mixes all three styles).
findings.proposal: Introduce in metal_ops.rs: `fn metal_tensor(t: &Tensor, what: &str) -> Result<(std::sync::RwLockReadGuard<Storage>, Layout)>` + `fn buf_off(ms: &MetalStorage, l: &Layout) -> (&Buffer, usize)` computing the byte offset from `dtype().size_in_bytes()`; `struct Dispatch<'a>` wrapping the encoder with `.pipeline(name)`, `.input(idx, buf, off)`, `.output(idx, buf)`, `.bytes(idx, &T)`, `.grid_1d(n, tg)`, `.grid(MTLSize, MTLSize)`; `fn out_storage(device, n, dtype, label) -> Result<(Arc<Buffer>, MetalStorage)>`; and a `metal_only_op!(Name, "label")` macro that emits `name()` and the `cpu_fwd` bail. Port the six in-scope ops first as the template (they are the simplest).
findings.expected_benefit: ~700-900 lines removed file-wide (≈35% of impl code; ~150 of the 507 in scope), one place to get byte offsets right, and a new op becomes ~30 lines of validation + one Dispatch chain. No runtime change.
findings.verify_how: Mechanical: `cargo test --features metal` on the M5 stays green and `git diff --stat` on metal_ops.rs shows the removed lines; the existing parity tests (mxfp4, sink, F8, owned) pin behaviour while porting.

verdict.reason: Counts check out (26 `impl CustomOp/InplaceOp` blocks, 24 `Storage::Metal(ms) => ms.buffer()` arms, 7 `Metal-only` bails in this file by grep) and the six in-scope ops do repeat the same encoder/dispatch idiom. But no latent bug is demonstrated: the F8Gemv offsets at 6650-6652 (`*2` for BF16 x, none for U8 bytes, `*4` for F32 scales) are each correct, and the 'next copy goes wrong' is hypothetical. A file-wide port of 26 ops is M effort with Metal-only verification for a zero-runtime-change refactor, which is polish by the task's own scale.
verdict.corrected_benefit: Fewer lines to read when adding a format; byte-offset arithmetic in one place. No runtime change.
verdict.corrected_proposal: Add only `fn buf_off(ms: &MetalStorage, l: &Layout) -> (&Buffer, usize)` (offset from `ms.dtype().size_in_bytes()`) and a `metal_only_op!` macro for `name()`/`cpu_fwd`, and apply them opportunistically to ops that findings 2, 3, 5 and 10 already touch; do not schedule a standalone 26-op port.

findings.title: The decode-GEMV batch cap is spelled four independent ways (literal 8, GGUF_BATCH_MAX, MPP_MATVEC_MAX_M, kernel acc[8]) and the F8 kernel trusts the caller
findings.evidence: metal_ops.rs:6598 `if k != self.in_features || m == 0 || m > 8 {` (F8Gemv, literal); moe.rs:109 `if (1..=8).contains(&m) && x.device().is_metal()` (literal, duplicated gate); metal_ops.rs:6387 `pub const GGUF_BATCH_MAX: usize = 8;` used by Mxfp4Matmul (6753); metal_ops.rs:3004 `const MPP_MATVEC_MAX_M: usize = 8;`; quant_kernels.metal:702 `#define GGUF_BATCH_MAX 8` and :3839 `float acc[8] = {0.0f};` with `for (uint r = 0; r < p.m; ++r)` (:3848) bounded only by the host-side literal. ROADMAP 'Constant and flag audit' D2 lists GGUF_BATCH_MAX as a threshold needing its measured crossover.
findings.rationale: Raising one copy (e.g. to let 9-16 concurrent sequences stay on the GEMV) silently leaves the others: moe.rs would route m=9 to the dequant path while F8Gemv bails, or, if only the Rust literal is raised, `f8_gemv_batch_bf16` indexes past `acc[8]`. The kernel has no `min(p.m, 8)` guard unlike the MXFP4 kernel (:3126 `min(p.m_batch, (uint)GGUF_BATCH_MAX)`).
findings.proposal: One `pub const DECODE_GEMV_MAX_M: usize = 8` in metal_ops.rs used by F8Gemv, Mxfp4Matmul, `Fp8Cached::forward`, `MppOwnedMatvec`'s MPP_MATVEC_MAX_M; in the shader a single `#define DECODE_GEMV_MAX_M 8` sizing `acc[]` and clamping `p.m`; a doc comment carrying the measured crossover per kernel as ROADMAP D2 asks (one run of the batch-scaling probe gives it).
findings.expected_benefit: Removes a latent out-of-bounds on the F8 batch kernel and makes the crossover a single measured knob; no runtime change today.
findings.verify_how: grep for `8` caps after the change; run the decode batch tests at m = DECODE_GEMV_MAX_M and +1 for both F8 and MXFP4.

findings.title: F8 experts fall off a 3x byte cliff at m = 9: full BF16 dequant per projection per call instead of a batched or tiled path
findings.evidence: metal_ops.rs:6708-6710 `pub fn f8_block_dequant_bf16(bytes, scales) -> Result<Tensor> { bytes.apply_op2_no_bwd(scales, &F8BlockDequantBf16) }` allocating `device.new_buffer(n, DType::BF16, ...)` for the whole weight (6512). Caller moe.rs:107-113: `if (1..=8).contains(&m) && ... { return f8_gemv(...) } self.linear()?.forward(x)` where `linear()` (100-103) builds a fresh `Linear` from the dequantized tensor on every call. F8Gemv itself refuses m > 8 (6598-6603). The MXFP4 sibling instead has a tiled kernel for m > 8 (`Mxfp4MulMM`, 6857-6927) that dequantizes strips in threadgroup memory.
findings.rationale: For an expert projection of out x in bytes B, the GEMV reads B; the m>8 path writes 2B (BF16), then the GEMM reads 2B plus x: ~4B of traffic and a transient 2B allocation per projection per call. On the prefill sparse path every routed expert in every layer takes this route once per prefill chunk (3 projections x 32 experts x all layers of full dequants), and under continuous batching any decode step where >8 sequences share an expert does too. The dequantized weights are dropped right after use, so nothing amortises them within a forward.
findings.proposal: Either (a) an F8 `mul_mm` with the same strip-dequant structure as `mxfp4_mul_mm_bf16` (replace `mxfp4_dequant_strip_into` with the F8 LUT decode and the block-scale lookup), routed from `Fp8Cached::forward` for m > DECODE_GEMV_MAX_M, or (b) cheaper: have `Fp8Cached` dequantize once per forward pass and cache the BF16 `Linear` for the duration of that step (clear at the end of the layer), so prefill pays 2B once per expert per step rather than per chunk and call. (a) is the real fix; (b) is a day.
findings.expected_benefit: Prefill TTFT on streamed FP8 MoE (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8) and batched decode above 8 sequences; traffic per expert projection drops from ~4B to ~B-2B, and the transient 2B allocations (tens of MB each, hundreds per step) stop churning candle's pool.
findings.verify_how: Instrument `Fp8Cached::forward` to count dequant calls per prefill on the 35B probe with a 2k-token prompt; measure TTFT before/after; the existing `fp8_resident_expert_matches_standard` test guards parity.

verdict.reason: Mechanism is real: moe.rs:100-113 builds a fresh `Linear` from `f8_block_dequant_bf16` on every call with m > 8 (F8Gemv bails above 8 at 6598-6603), the dequant allocates the whole BF16 weight (6512), and `dispatch_sparse` (moe.rs:603-650) feeds each expert all its routed tokens, so prefill m per expert exceeds 8 for any prompt beyond a few dozen tokens. But the only models on this path are streamed FP8 MoE experts (`Fp8Cached` exists for expert_stream; a 35B-A3B FP8 checkpoint cannot be resident on 24 GB), and a prefill that touches every expert is bound by `fetch_many`'s SSD reads of those same experts (expert_stream.rs:230-250), which move the same B bytes at a rate tens of times slower than the extra ~3B of device traffic. Decode steps with >8 sequences sharing one expert are rare on a streamed model. So the cost is real but hidden on the supported configuration.
verdict.corrected_benefit: Removes transient 2B BF16 allocations per expert projection per prefill chunk (pool churn) and some device traffic that is currently hidden behind SSD fetch time; measurable only on a resident FP8 MoE, which no supported 24 GB configuration runs.
verdict.corrected_proposal: Option (b) only, and only after instrumenting `Fp8Cached::forward` shows dequant time is visible next to fetch time on the 35B probe: cache the dequantized `Linear` for the duration of one forward step. Skip the F8 mul_mm kernel unless a resident FP8 MoE becomes a target.

findings.title: MXFP4 prefill matmul is a naive 16x16 one-output-per-thread tile with device x reads inside the K loop
findings.evidence: metal_ops.rs:6910-6921 dispatch `width: self.n.div_ceil(GGUF_MM_BN), height: m.div_ceil(GGUF_MM_BM)` with TG `16 x 16` (GGUF_MM_BM/BN = 16 at 6705-6708); 6943 routes every `m > GGUF_BATCH_MAX` here. quant_kernels.metal:3197-3246: `threadgroup bfloat w_tile[GGUF_MM_BN][MXFP4_BLOCK]; ... for (uint b = 0; b < nb; ++b) { mxfp4_dequant_strip_into(...); threadgroup_barrier; if (m < M && n < N) { device const bfloat *x_chunk = x + m*K + b*32; for (j < 32) partial += (float)x_chunk[j] * (float)w_tile[n_off][j]; } threadgroup_barrier; }` — each thread computes one output, x is re-read from device by all 16 n-lanes of a row, two barriers per 32-wide K step, no simdgroup matrix ops. ROADMAP 'Performance backlog' lists 'MXFP4 prefill' under the TensorOps/MPP roadmap (planned, not rejected).
findings.rationale: For gpt-oss prefill every expert's gate_up (N=5760, K=2880) and down run through this; arithmetic intensity per barrier pair is 8,192 FMAs with 512 scalar threadgroup stores, and at M = 9..16 the single M-tile idles up to 7/16 of its threads. The F8 path and every other format reach candle/MPP GEMMs for large M; MXFP4 is the only format whose prefill GEMM is hand-rolled and untiled in registers.
findings.proposal: Shortest path: add `mxfp4_dequant_bf16` (elementwise mirror of `f8_block_dequant_bf16`, 40 lines) and route `m > DECODE_GEMV_MAX_M` through `Linear`/MPP GEMM exactly as `Fp8Cached::linear()` does, dropping Mxfp4MulMM; or, if the 2x transient weight is unwanted on 24 GB, keep the tiled kernel but use `simdgroup_matrix` 8x8 bf16 tiles with x staged in threadgroup memory (the mpp_gemm.metal staged path already has the IQ strip-dequant + TensorOps structure to copy).
findings.expected_benefit: gpt-oss-20b TTFT; the staged GEMM shipped TTFT -23/27% on other formats and this kernel is further from peak than those were. Also smooths the m=9 step (GEMV at m=8 reads the weight once; the tile at m=9 reads it once too but at ~1/4 the ALU efficiency).
findings.verify_how: Clone `staged_quant_crossover_probe` for MXFP4 at M in {8, 16, 64, 256, 1024}, N=5760, K=2880; report GFLOP/s for Mxfp4MulMM vs dequant+candle matmul vs dequant+MPP; A/B gpt-oss TTFT on a 2k prompt.

verdict.reason: Kernel verified at metal:3197-3246: 16x16 TG, one output per thread, `w_tile[16][32]` strip dequant then `threadgroup_barrier`, each thread reads its 32 `x_chunk[j]` values from device memory inside the K loop (so the 16 n-lanes of a row re-read the same 64 bytes), a second barrier per 32-wide K step, no simdgroup matrix ops; dispatch at 6910-6921 with GGUF_MM_BM/BN = 16 (6705-6708) and every m > 8 routed here (6943). gpt-oss-20b is resident on the M5, so this is on the TTFT critical path for every expert in every layer during prefill. ROADMAP lists 'MXFP4 prefill' under the TensorOps/MPP roadmap (planned), nothing rejects it. Cheapest sound route: the per-expert BF16 transient (gate_up 5760x2880 x 2 B = 33 MB) is affordable, so an elementwise dequant plus the existing MPP GEMM (crossover documented at MPP_GEMM_MIN_M=64) gets most of the win; the cleaner route is to add MXFP4 as a `WeightKind` (metal_ops.rs:2887-2900, kernel names at 2981) so `mpp_owned_matmul`'s staged strip-dequant GEMM serves it with no transient at all. Severity medium / effort M are fair.

findings.title: Per-dispatch host overhead: global pipeline mutex + hash lookup, 2-3 Tensor clones and RwLock reads per expert GEMV call
findings.evidence: metal_ops.rs:6687-6693 `x.apply_op1_no_bwd(&F8Gemv { bytes: bytes.clone(), scales: scales.clone(), ... })` and 6944-6951 three `clone()`s per mxfp4 call; inside metal_fwd `self.bytes.storage_and_layout()` / `self.scales.storage_and_layout()` (6631-6632; 6788-6808 x3) each take a RwLock read; `get_or_compile_quant_pipeline` (1596-1609) locks a global `Mutex<HashMap<(u64,&str), ComputePipeline>>` and clones the pipeline (ObjC retain/release) on every call; `self.bytes.shape().dims2()?` / `self.scales.shape().dims2()?` re-validate static weight geometry per call (6605-6606).
findings.rationale: gpt-oss issues ~192 expert GEMVs per token and FP8 MoE ~288; each pays the mutex + hash + retain and the clone/lock churn on the engine thread that also encodes everything else. Individually microseconds, collectively a fraction of a millisecond per token: small, but free to remove and it sits on the same thread as the launch-bound work in findings 2-3.
findings.proposal: Cache the resolved `ComputePipeline` in the owning layer (`Mxfp4Linear`, `Fp8Cached`) in a `OnceLock<ComputePipeline>` and pass it in the op struct; store `(buffer, byte_offset)` of the static weight tensors once at construction instead of `storage_and_layout()` per call (safe because the owning struct holds the Tensor alive); take `&Tensor` in the op structs instead of cloning (CustomOp1 only needs `'static` for `apply_op1`, not for `apply_op1_no_bwd` with a borrowed op).
findings.expected_benefit: Sub-1% decode on MoE models; removes one global lock from the per-token path, which also matters if a second model's engine thread shares the device.
findings.verify_how: `OXYDLLM_PROFILE_DECODE` host-side encode time per token before/after on gpt-oss-20b; or `cargo flamegraph` of the engine thread during decode and look for `get_or_compile_quant_pipeline` + `RwLock::read`.
